issue.title: Add child_process.spawnShell
issue.body:
In the child_process module currently there is two flavors of exec function: exec and execFile, which is good, but for spawn, there is only one version, would've been great to have something like child_process.spawnShell. Currently I use this code to emulate it:
```javascript
child_process.spawn('cmd', ['/s', '/c', command], {windowsVerbatimArguments:true})
```
but it is platform specific and requires the use of undocumented flag windowsVerbatimArguments

comment.body:
If I understood the question correctly, what he wants a way to spawn a shell without running any commands.

I can't see the a big use case for this since you anyway need to run different commands in windows and unix. What I'm saying is that you probably need the if which this will remove from your code anyway.

The only benefit would be that you don't need to use the undocumented `windowsVerbatimArguments` flag. Maybe a better solution is to document that?

Yeh, I know.

> Unrelated to your pull, but I'm just pointing it out. :)

issue.title: Friendly fire fixes and sam sites
issue.body:
This PR will fix the following issues:

https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/issues/7442

^ is solved by clearing the turret activities when not being able to attack (during low power).

https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/issues/7403

^ is being solved by clearing the targets when the owner is changed.

comment.body:
I can confirm that this fixes #7403. I cannot reproduce #7442 at all, so can't confim the fix there. I did notice a huge regression with AttackMove and subsequent Move orders due to that fix, though.

* With AttackMove, the unit's movement isn't fluid, they stop at least once per second and then resume along their path immediately.
* After an AttackMove has finished, turreted units will ignore Move commands. They'll react to another AttackMove command, though.

issue.title: config for Adam
issue.body:
I'm trying to use the implementation of the adam optimizer available in the `optim` package with the line

`-- not used -- x, batchlowerbound = optim.adagrad(opfunc, parameters, config, state)`
`x, batchlowerbound = optim.adam(opfunc, parameters, config, state)`

It does not seem to converge or even change much with any of the configurations I've tried.

Could you suggest a `config` which works please?

Thank you.

comment.body:
Hi Joost, 

unfortunately I have'nt managed to get any convergence yet with adam, over a range of different config parameters? 

Looking at figure 4 a) of the [adam paper](http://arxiv.org/pdf/1412.6980v2.pdf), it seems that 

beta_1 = 0.1
beta_2 = 0.0001
alpha = 0.002
epsilon = 1e-8
lambda = 1 - 1e-8 

with the model they state,

dim_hidden = 50
hidden_units_encoder = 500
hidden_units_decoder = 500

should get convergence after after 10 epochs, but I can't reproduce their results?

return sequence.toString(); // indent:8 ; exp:8; ok
} // indent:6 ; exp:6; ok

private void checkNotNull(CharSequence replacement) {}
```

pull_request.title: Improve code coverage for System.Diagnostics.Debug
pull_request.body:
Primary changes:
- The AttributeTests class wasn't public, and thus none of its tests were being run.  Fixed it to be public, and fixed one of its tests that was throwing ~4 billion exceptions and thus taking a very long time to run :)
- Added coverage for DebuggerTypeProxyAttribute, which was left out of the tests
- (Potentially controversial) The current testing is done against a test mock.  This means that while the Debug API is being exercised, the actual underlying implementation is not.  I added a call to exercise that underlying implementation as well, just to ensure it's not failing, but no verification is done on its output.
- Added stubbed out tests for Debugger, which is currently not implemented.  This will help ensure we go back and add tests when the real implementation is available.
- Added tests for a few other corner cases

This boosts the code coverage of the tests from ~40% to ~67%.  We are unlikely to get much higher than this: the remaining missed code paths are either related to resources or to popping up assert modal dialogs, which we don't want to do in tests.

issue.title: sys/udp: Checksum calculation broken
issue.body:
UDP packet handling no longer works because the [checksum calculation in udp.c](https://github.com/RIOT-OS/RIOT/blob/master/sys/net/transport_layer/udp/udp.c#L82) fails. Reverting in the master history, the problem was introduced with the merge of #2497.

The problem can for example be reproduced using the rpl_udp example:
Sending:
>send fe80::ff:fe00:afee hello
>Successful deliverd 28 bytes over UDP to ff02::1 to 6LoWPAN

But on the receiver side it fails:
>IPv6 datagram received (next header: 11) from fe80::200:ff:fe00:afee 
>Wrong checksum (2)!

comment.body: @fnack can you provide a packet capture? The source address is wrong on the receiving end, which gives the wrong checksum (2), we need to check whether the error is in the reception or transmission

issue.title: Improve code coverage for System.Diagnostics.Debug
issue.body:
Primary changes:
- The AttributeTests class wasn't public, and thus none of its tests were being run.  Fixed it to be public, and fixed one of its tests that was throwing ~4 billion exceptions and thus taking a very long time to run :)
- Added coverage for DebuggerTypeProxyAttribute, which was left out of the tests
- (Potentially controversial) The current testing is done against a test mock.  This means that while the Debug API is being exercised, the actual underlying implementation is not.  I added a call to exercise that underlying implementation as well, just to ensure it's not failing, but no verification is done on its output.
- Added stubbed out tests for Debugger, which is currently not implemented.  This will help ensure we go back and add tests when the real implementation is available.
- Added tests for a few other corner cases

This boosts the code coverage of the tests from ~40% to ~67%.  We are unlikely to get much higher than this: the remaining missed code paths are either related to resources or to popping up assert modal dialogs, which we don't want to do in tests.

issue.title: Web front end can't find files for tests
issue.body:
I've just set up a test deployment of Fedora's openQA set up on a local system. It's mostly working, but all the features which rely on openQA being able to find files in the `testresults` directory don't seem to be working:

* I don't get a live log or live view while the tests are running
* I don't get a list of result files for a finished test
* I don't see thumbnails for each test step on a finished test (but I do see screenshots when I enter an individual test step)

Comparing to our production deployment where all this stuff works, I see what looks to be a significant difference. On our production deployment, the breadcrumb trail looks something like this:

openQA > Test results > fedora-rawhide-server-x86_64-Build22_Alpha_TC7-server_simple_encrypted

(i.e., whatever's considered the 'test name' for that display does not include the test number). But on my deployment it looks like this:

openQA > Test results > 00000011-fedora-rawhide-server-x86_64-Build22_Alpha_TC7-server_firewall_disabled

The test number *is* included, there.

however, for *both* deployments, the `testresults` subdirectory names have the test number in them. On my deployment I have:

`/var/lib/openqa/testresults/00000011-fedora-rawhide-server-x86_64-Build22_Alpha_TC7-server_firewall_disabled`

and on the working deployment there is:

`/var/lib/openqa/testresults/00000081-fedora-rawhide-server-x86_64-Build22_Alpha_TC7-server_simple_encrypted`

So I think there's probably some kind of mismatch somewhere and the server's probably looking for the files in `/var/lib/openqa/testresults/00000011-00000011-fedora-rawhide-server-x86_64-Build22_Alpha_TC7-server_firewall_disabled` or something like that, and that's why it can't find them? But I'm no perl expert and have no experience with Mojolicious, so I haven't been able to pin down exactly where the problem is, unfortunately.

  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/ssl.py", line 364, in wrap_socket
    _context=self)
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/ssl.py", line 578, in __init__
    self.do_handshake()
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/ssl.py", line 805, in do_handshake
    self._sslobj.do_handshake()
ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:600)

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
[... snip ...]
```

comment.body:
I think it shouldn't be too hard to do, all of the 1024 bit roots are gone now, so diff the before and after bundles and check the bit size of the root, if it's 1024 bit then just hardcode that certificate ID as a removed for 1024 bit.

You already have that trap, for example browsers will fetch intermediate certificates if mentioned in the AIA where requests will not. I don't think it's reasonable for requests to keep these certificates long term. Mozilla is no longer going to be paying attention to them so they are essentially not going to have anyone looking at them to decide if they should still be trusted or not. It's starting to veer off into the territory of requests adding its own root certificates.

issue.body:
Hello. I got the following message trying to run lesson 2 of lamda.
```
[Error] Critical: Found two modules with the same name: SUBSTITUTION
        Source: File: k\include\modules\substitution.k
        Location: (158,1,298,9)
```
The other substitution module is in substitution-java.k

In my project, I was having a problem with substitution, so I tried running the simplest example, and I got that message even though kompiling my project does not produce it.

comment.body:
The problem I'm having in my project is that it is not substituting a sort that I created. I tried to reduce/simplify the rule so that it works. Here it is:
`rule func(Body:Exp, P:Param) => Body[0/P]`
where Param can only be a `CamelCaseId`, the sort that I created imitating K's builtin `Id`. Here it is:
```
module CCID-SYNTAX-HOOKS
	syntax CamelCaseId ::= Token{[a-z][\_a-zA-Z0-9]*}       
                 [notInRules, regex("(?<![A-Za-z0-9\\_])[a-z\\_][A-Za-z0-9\\_]*")]
endmodule

module CCID-HOOKS
  imports CCID-SYNTAX-HOOKS
  imports STRING-HOOKS
  imports K

	syntax String ::= "CamelCaseId2String" "(" CamelCaseId ")"         
		[function, hook(#CONVERSION:token2string), klabel(CamelCaseId2String)]
	syntax CamelCaseId ::= "String2CamelCaseId" "(" String ")"         
		[function, hook(#CONVERSION:string2id), klabel(String2CamelCaseId)]
	rule CamelCaseId2String(X:CamelCaseId) => #tokenToString(X)         [function,anywhere]
	rule String2CamelCaseId(S:String) => #parseToken("CamelCaseId", S)  [function,anywhere]

	syntax CamelCaseId ::= freshCamelCaseId(Int)	[freshGenerator, function]
	rule freshCamelCaseId(I:Int) => String2CamelCaseId("var_" +String Int2String(I))
endmodule
```
What happens is that the substitution gets stuck:
```
#substitute ( someExp , #patternMatch1 ( decomposeMatching`(_`,_`)(_`(_`)
   (#token("CamelCaseId","x"),.KList),_`(_`)(#_(0),.KList)) , .Map ) )
```

When I tried to convert my `Param` to `Id` and pass that to the substitution function, doing this:
```
  syntax Id ::= Param2Id(Param) [function]
  rule Param2Id(P:Param) => String2Id(#tokenToString(P)) [function,anywhere]
rule func(Body:Exp, P:Param) => Body[0/Param2Id(P)] [function]
``` 
When I do that, It acts as if it did substitute even though it does not. I know that because the rest of the rule is applied, but the substitution part is not.

```
I've done a little research into doing this with deck.js (one of the JQuery 
based HTML5 slide decks) and Pusher(http://pusher.com).

While a "naked" WebSockets experience would be preferable, I like what Pusher 
brings to the table in WebSockets + a concept of AMQP-like channels and 
concurrent synced connections. It also has a Java API that could birth a 
Android preso remote control. 

If you are doing a one-to-one relationship, speaker display as the master 
client and presentation display as the slave, could you not use the App Engine 
Channel API? The caveat being that it would tie you to AppEngine and be of 
reduced utility for some.
```

issue.title: Make logs more accessible
issue.body:
Currently most of the logs are hidden in the .meteor/local/log folder. We should make them more visible. To start with we should transfer them to a central place (velocity:core) into a MongoDB collection.

### Outputting logs

For outputting the logs I suggest a similar plugin system to the test result reporters.
Initially we would have these options:

* velocity:log-console-reporter (Output to console)
* velocity:html-reporter (Make probably sense to include it as part of the existing html-reporter)
* velocity:log-file-reporter (Output to file)

If someone has an alternative suggestion for the naming, let me know.

### Transferring logs

#### API

We should have a Meteor method in velocity:core for sending log lines from a testing framework to velocity:core.

A suggestion (still WiP):
```javascript
Meteor.call('velocity/logs/submit', {
  framework: 'my-framework',
  lines: [
    'Line 1',
    'Line 2'
  ]
})
```

* Assign log lines to a specific framework
* Allow to send multiple lines with one Meteor call (does this make a performance difference vs. one call per line?)

#### Mirror logs

Transfer stdout and stderr of mirrors to the main app.

issue.title: Hangs on confirming host key phase.
issue.body:
If host key hasn't yet been cached, the whole thing hangs. Or more precisely, it waits for you to type "yes<Enter>". But there's probably no way one can do it. Well, one can do it, or so it seems. You type "yes" and press `Enter`. And it looks like it got your answer. But no, it's not gonna progress any further.

The issue must be because `mina` [redirects `stdin`](https://github.com/mina-deploy/mina/blob/v0.3.2/lib/mina/exec_helpers.rb#L20), but `ssh` reads from `/dev/tty`. Not sure if there's anyting one can do.

comment.body:
We found a workaround for this, for now.
In the v0.3.2 you can use `mina ssh` command which will open a normal ssh where you can type yes.
Then disconnect and use setup/deploy

issue.title: Tracking units in the model and databases
issue.body: It might be helpful to have a method that tracks and checks units of numbers in the various databases. As it is currently set up, the measure JSON database includes a field to support strings denoting units. Units are not tracked in the microsegment data. While we can include units in the wiki, if new versions of the microsegment source data are reported in different units, there is no method currently in place to ensure that those changes will be detected and/or corrected. Additionally, units in measures are not necessarily standardized, and might require conversion for use in the model.

issue.title: Moving from indexeddb to sbot's levedb storage via the phoenix api
issue.body:
I began using level.js on indexeddb to store private user state such as "which messages have been read" and "which messages has the user subscribed to." I made that choice believing indexeddb was reliably persistent, but that turns out not to be the case. In https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-webapps/2013OctDec/0830.html they describe a "temporary storage" policy where a hard limit is enforced by ejecting the oldest writes. (Max Ogden, author of level.js, confirmed this.)

More related reading:
https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/forum/#!topic/chromium-html5/xtJ_uFeRs_U

And a bad sign that it's not going to be solved soon:
https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-webapps/2013OctDec/0980.html

The state I'm storing isn't critical, but it's not something users should ever have to lose. (Can you imagine if your inbox suddenly forgot which messages you've read? No sir!) 

I think the only logical solution is storage hosted by scuttlebot. We've talked in the past about adding a leveldb api to sbot for applications to use. I'm not yet sure if that's a good idea. We're still figuring out what kind of applications sbot will support, and a leveldb API opens up complex questions about permissions and resource usage quotas.

The alternative I'm going with (unless anybody objects strongly) is adding methods to `phoenix-api` for these features, eg `api.markRead(key, cb)`, `api.markUnread(key, cb)`, `api.isRead(key, cb)`, and so on. Internally, phoenix-api will store the data in sbot's leveldb instance. That way, we can get persistent storage, but don't go so far as to expose leveldb directly.

issue.title: Fix opencl rendering issues on Os X
issue.body:
Looks like Apple's opencl compiler is once again quite picky. All of the issues I was encountering stemmed from opencl compiler issues along the lines of
````
error: call to 'foo' is ambiguous
````

By explicitly specifying whether a floating-point literal is double or float, it tells the compiler which override to use when multiple precision definitions of a function are availble.

I also modified the opencl stuff to output program build errors to the info panel in Fractorium, so I could see what was going on. It's not copy-pastable but it shows where the problem is.

Change-Id: I9d7d0c04c488a35319253a30234403850baf9fb9

Don't expect [CLOSED] when mailbox gets invalidated prior to SELECT

The earlier fixes for handling of [CLOSED] were incomplete because they
failed to catch a situation where a mailbox gets replaced while the
SELECT is still pending. This happened when e.g. someone decided to open
a mailbox (SELECT on the way) right after switching to online from
offline, a switching which triggered LIST and therefore mailbox
replacement.

A fix for this is to reset the connection state when UNSELECT (or an
equivalent) completes.

issue.title: Eating from stack removes all with replace_with_item
issue.body:
Eating from a stack of mushroom soup or hearty stew replaces the whole stack with a single bowl which isnt too good, so I've redone the routine within hunger.lua to add the replace_with_item to the inventory if space is available or drop as an item if not...

```
function hud.item_eat(hunger_change, replace_with_item, poisen, heal)
	return function(itemstack, user, pointed_thing)
	
		if itemstack:take_item() ~= nil and user ~= nil then
		
			local name = user:get_player_name()
			local h = tonumber(hud.hunger[name])
			local hp = user:get_hp()
			local rm = false
			local msg = nil

			-- Healing
			if hp < 20 and heal then
				hp = hp + heal
				if hp > 20 then hp = 20 end
				user:set_hp(hp)
				rm = true
				msg = ""
			elseif hp == 20 and heal then
				msg = "You already have full health"
			end

			-- Hunger
			if h < 30 and hunger_change then
				h = h + hunger_change
				if h > 30 then h = 30 end
				hud.hunger[name]=h
				hud.set_hunger(user)
				rm = true
			elseif h>= 30 and hunger_change and not msg then
				msg = "Cannot eat, not hungry"
			end
			
			if msg then minetest.chat_send_player(user:get_player_name(), msg) end
			
			-- Poison
			if poisen then
				poisenp(1.0, poisen, 0, user)
			end

			-- if item eaten and replace_with_item, check if inventory full, add/drop replacement
			if rm then
				local inv = user:get_inventory()
				if inv:room_for_item("main", {name=replace_with_item}) then
					inv:add_item("main", replace_with_item)
				else
					local pos = user:getpos()
					pos.y = math.floor(pos.y + 0.5)
					core.add_item(pos, replace_with_item)
				end

				return itemstack
			end
			
		end
	end
end

pull_request.title: WIP: Add tolerance for equality when optimizing ticks (Fix #550)
pull_request.body:
The main problem is in the [computation](https://github.com/dcjones/Gadfly.jl/blob/404f0aa433fa5431ba377234bd6d3427e9c174ab/src/ticks.jl#L93)

```julia
r = ceil((x_max - span) / (q*10.0^z * one_t))
```

where `z` is basically `log10(x_max - x_min)`.  If `x_max - x_min` is very small, `r` becomes too large.  Using `eps()` as the tolerance just happens to fix the failing example listed in #550, it is still too low for other examples.  For example:

```julia
y = ones(5)
y[1] = 1 + 2eps()

plot(x = 1:5, y = y, Geom.point)
```

will result in an infinite [loop](https://github.com/dcjones/Gadfly.jl/blob/404f0aa433fa5431ba377234bd6d3427e9c174ab/src/ticks.jl#L94)

@dcjones, any thoughts on how we can pick a reasonable tolerance?

listed in #550.  It is probably still too small though. The main problem
is actually in the computation

```
r = ceil((x_max - span) / (q*10.0^z * one_t))
```

where `z` is basically `log10(x_max - x_min)`.  If `x_max - x_min`
is very small, `r` becomes very large.

We need the copy to allow for altering active[key] while iterating. But the normal removeFunc tests for identity. The problem is if it's not a FunctionList, but just an AbstractMessageMatcher.

issue.title: (Proposal) Make Multiple PeekAheadChar( ) Comparisions simpler
issue.body:
In the [scanner](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/master/src/Compilers/VisualBasic/Portable/Scanner/Scanner.vb#L1495) there are multiple occasions where we compare the results of multipe calls to `PeekAheadChar` against the characters of a desired sequence of characters. In essences do the following character match this string.
**Example**
```vb
If CanGetCharAtOffset(length + 8) AndAlso 
    PeekAheadChar(length + 2) = "C"c AndAlso
    PeekAheadChar(length + 3) = "D"c AndAlso 
    PeekAheadChar(length + 4) = "A"c AndAlso 
    PeekAheadChar(length + 5) = "T"c AndAlso 
    PeekAheadChar(length + 6) = "A"c AndAlso 
    PeekAheadChar(length + 7) = "["c Then 
        Return XmlMakeBeginCDataToken(precedingTrivia, scanTrailingTrivia) 
End If 
```
It would make the code much simpler if this was abstracted in to a function.
I propose the functon name of **NextAre** as it scans good with current conditionals (of If / When)

```vb
If NextAre(8,2,"CDATA[") Then Return XmlMakeBeginCDataToken(precedingTrivia, scanTrailingTrivia)
```
```vb
Case "["c When NextAre(8,2,"CDATA[")  :  Return XmlMakeBeginCDataToken(precedingTrivia, scanTrailingTrivia)
```

--------

**Implementation**

```vb
Function NextAre( at As Integer , text As String ) As Boolean
  Return NextAre( at,1,text)
End Function

Function NextAre( at As Integer, start As Integer, text As String ) As Boolean
  If text Is Nothing Then Return False
  Dim n = word.length
  If Not CanGetCharAtOffset( at+n ) Then Return False
  Dim startAt = at + start
  Dim i=0
  While i < n
    If PeekAheadChar( startAt+i ) <> text( i ) Then Return False
    i+=1
  End While
  Return True
End Function
```
**Note:** ```start + text.Length = at``` seems to hold true, which if that is the case then the parameters of the function can be reduced to two. ```( start As Integer, text As String ) As Boolean``` 
So is there any existing use case (in roslyn) where this isn't the case.

comment.body:
@AdamSpeight2008 Thanks for the suggestion. We welcome suggestions from anyone whether experienced or novice.

I like the NextAre/PeekAheadString idea and I agree that it would simplify plenty of callsites in the VB scanner. Performance aside, it's easier to read, easier to comprehend and easier to check for correctness, so it scores well for code maintenance.
Performance-wise, in most places it's not going to be on critical path since the scanner goes one char at a time and only does the 'peek ahead string' once a common prefix has been determined. However, there's probably a second-order benefit: By replacing the sequence of char-by-char comparisons with a single method call ('outlining'), the IL and, indirectly, the generated code has been simplified and shortened, making the critical path code shorter and that means fewer L1 cache misses. This will be hard to measure except in dedicated micro-benchmarks for the VB parser (we have one, but I doubt it's sensitive enough for this change.)

I don't like the recursive implementation. Roslyn, at present, never emits the tail recursion IL instruction, and I don't think the JIT will make the transform either. I don't think using recursion adds anything to readability either.

issue.title: New Features Introduction
issue.body:
The new release has so many new features, players might be overwhelmed/not notice them all. I thought it might be good to put together a small tutorial that introduces them to the new features. The parameters are:

- It would be an askChoice function where each button gives information about a specific feature

- It will appear automatically the first time the player opens a game with the new version (and ONLY then), and afterwards will be available via a menu command

- It will make use of the textFunctions script to store all the tutorial text in a .txt file, which we can modify for future releases to explain functions for those

- Basically, it is a sort of in-game interactive changelog explaining how to use the latest game features

I'm not sure what the best thing to name it would be, though.

issue.title: "Performance Wins for Your Mobile App"
issue.body:
```

Fragments for screen resolutions: come up with framework for different 
resolutions.

"Time-to-text" on mobile is important. Load things lazily (don't display images 
/content that may never be seen. @font-face keeps text invisible while font 
downloads.

Minimize browser reflows: If you make complex rendering changes such as 
animations, do so out of the flow. Use position-absolute or position-fixed to 
accomplish this.

document.createDocumentFragment()
dataURIs
css selectors (read from right to left -> no decendant selectors, ids are best)
css3 3d transforms for animations instead of el.style.top/el.style.left
gzip, js/css compressions
combine css/jss
sprites
hiding/unhiding containers instead of creating them on the fly?
Be smart about DOM manipulations: e.g. reduce browser repaints
new ECMASCript methods (querySelector, array methods, etc.) instead of libs.
```

issue.body:
![screen shot 2015-02-26 at 3 06 07 pm](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/230875/6400729/077bb168-bdc9-11e4-9ac8-ac98fcb35343.png)

As you can see, the text within the EditText (A MaterialMultiAutoCompleteTextView, in this case) is being clipped rather dramatically. I believe it's being caused by the floating label, but I can't prove it. The floating label itself is turned off, and I've tested with several other variables, including setting the Paddings to 0. But nothing seems to help this clipping.

Any suggestions?

comment.body:
Hi @gtcompscientist ,

You're right. This is due to the floating label. Why not just hide the floating label or increase the wrapper layout's height?

issue.title: make sure that toggle sidebar class works properly
issue.body:
This PR will:
- make sure that toggle sidebar class works properly
- fix issue when printing and sidebar-collapse still occupies the space
- fix content-wrapper height when expanding treeview menu.
   - this pushes the footer in relation to sidebar's new height
- add initial body class for sidebar toggle function to work well

comment.body: I see the problem now. After a few tests, I noticed the sidebar hides only if the sidebar-collapse class is applied and the sidebar-open is not. The goal that we want to achieve is to have the printing work weather these classes are there or not. I think the way to do that is via CSS. I am currently making this my priority since the template promises an enhanced printing experience.

commits.message:
Add/remove some MinWise constructors.

Remove the constructor that initialized a new MinWise instance
from a set of string integer (e.g., "123") data.  This was nothing
other than a for loop basically.

Add the constructor NewMinWiseFromSignature to convert from []uint64
to a MinWise instance.  This allows for further streaming when loading
a signature from saved data, provided the original hash functions used
to create the signature in the first place are known.

issue.title: Shader documentation
issue.body: Can a bit of documentation be provided for the shader logic? Specifically I'm interested in the logical behind some of the constants in `physicalColor` of `main.html` and how I could modify them if I wanted.

comment.body:
The physical color scaling is partitioning the full 0...1  range into seven evenly spaced sub-ranges. That's what the modulo and floor are doing. Then, each range modifies only one color channel while keeping the other two constant. This is done in such a way that no two different values map to the same color.

The ranges are:
1. black (0,0,0) to red (1,0,0)
2. red (1,0,0) to yellow (1,1,0)
3. yellow (1,1,0) to green (0,1,0)
4. green (0,1,0) to cyan (0,1,1)
5. cyan (0,1,1) to blue (0,0,1)
6. blue (0,0,1) to magenta (1,0,1)
7. magenta (1,0,1) to white (1,1,1)

issue.title: New visualization mode
issue.body:
Right now the view of the cells is pretty basic: all live cells are represented by the same character (*). Cells born in the current generation are drawn in green, others in white.

Here's a more fancy visualization mode:
- use different characters according to the "fate" of the cell: will it die of isolation, overcrowding, or will it survive?
- use different colors according to the age of the cell: e.g. different colors for cells born 0, 1, 2, 5+, 10+ generations ago

This requires changes in the game implementations to compute and keep track of these new informations (fates and ages).

issue.title: hash MutableDenseMatrix
issue.body:
Addition of Trace(X) returned TypeError when X was
MutableDenseMatrix. This was because MutableDenseMatrix
wasn't hashable. This has been fixed by introducing
hashable_content function for Trace. This function
returns sympify(X) which is hashable and hence making
MutableDenseMatrix hashable.

Fixes: #9043

comment.body: This fix is wrong. mutableDenseMatrix *shouldn't* be hashable, since it's mutable. The fix is to call sympify in the constrictor of Trace, which will convert a mutable matrix to an immutable one.

commits.message:
Ensure exceptions from methodBlock() don't result in unrooted tests.

The introduction of the runLeaf() method in BlockJUnit4ClassRunner in
JUnit 4.9 introduced a regression with regard to exception handling.

Specifically, the invocation of methodBlock() is no longer executed
within a try-catch block as was the case in previous versions of JUnit.

Custom modifications to methodBlock() or the methods it invokes may in
fact throw exceptions. In such cases, exceptions thrown from
methodBlock() cause the current test execution to abort immediately. As
a result, the failing test method is unrooted in test reports, and
subsequent test methods are never invoked. Furthermore, RunListeners
registered with JUnit are not notified.

This commit addresses this issue by wrapping the invocation of
methodBlock() within a try-catch block. If an exception is not thrown,
the resulting Statement is passed to runLeaf(). If an exception is
thrown, it is wrapped in a Fail statement which is passed to runLeaf().

Closes #1066
Closes #1082

issue.title: Tweak Modernizr blurb in "mobifying" post.
issue.body:
```
In the "mobifying" post you wrote:

"Modernizr is great, but it runs a bunch of tests on every load. Some of those 
tests make costly modifications to the DOM and slows down page load."

I performed a series of tests over the cost of pre DOM load feature testing 
(like those in Modernizr), and found there to be little-to-no cost from reflow. 
I also did a series of screencasts exploring the cost of feature testing and 
found that even on slow portable devices, like the Kindle, feature testing 
performed relatively well. 

I do agree with your last sentence though:
"Now, we're only including these libraries on pages where they're actually 
needed. -2 requests :)"

http://allyoucanleet.com/2011/02/05/the-cost-of-feature-testing/
http://allyoucanleet.com/2011/02/17/the-cost-of-pre-dom-load-reflow/
```

commits.message:
Recents long press: add pluggable implementation

- Adds a Secure.Setting for the activity component to handle
  Intent.ACTION_RECENTS_LONG_PRESS.
- Adds a new intent ACTION_RECENTS_LONG_PRESS for the
  long press of the recents button. Other system applications
  can register for the intent to provide custom handling.
  Handlers of this intent are queried for in the settings
  application, and if no handlers are found, the default
  implementation falls back on ActionUtils.switchToLastApp().

  The long press listener on the recents button is replaced
  with a touch handler to allow for more custom handling.

For cm-12.0, the following modifications were made:

- With the full deprecation of ActivityManager.getRecentTasks(),
  applications can not query for the last foreground application.
  To aid these applications, the framework will include an
  EXTRA_CURRENT_PACKAGE_NAME with ACTION_RECENTS_LONG_PRESS.
- Instead of re-evaluating packages on every Long Press, PhoneStatusBar
  now tracks Settings changes and package activities and
  incrementally caches the desired Recents long press behavior.

This is a roll-up CR from cm-11.0, and also contains the following Change-Ids:
- I689e8b5c26b39e100cb166d2f93e7ee49e83f93a

Change-Id: I8a27ae0fe58d92a1626f0bd661c5f57c589fac17

Conflicts:

	core/java/android/provider/Settings.java
	packages/SystemUI/src/com/android/systemui/statusbar/phone/PhoneStatusBar.java

issue.title: CSS positioning in the middle, wrong info
issue.body:
```
Please describe the issue:

The flexbox tutorial states: "Centering something horizontally and vertically 
has long been a challenge in CSS. The best CSS-only solution we have is 
position:absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; paired with negative left/top margins 
that equal half of the width/height. And that only flies with explicitly sized 
elements."

This is not correct.
There is a way, based on display:table-cell; which is at least 6 years old 
(Dušan Janovský wrote about it in 2004), to align vertically. I've documented 
the full horizontal & vertical solution here:
http://james.gameover.com/index.php/2009/vertically-centring-in-css-without-hack
s-and-multi-line-enabled/

It even works without explicitly sized elements.

PS. The negative margins solution is Ugh though, you're right about that.

```

issue.title: Long words are rendered over the right margin in justified paragraph(s)
issue.body:
Sometimes, a long word is rendered over the right margin. 

The word "insignificant" is rendered over the right margin in the below paragraph.

The macros \ldquo{} and \rdquo{} are for unicode U+201C and U+201D.


Example of paragraph that can cause this issue (excerpt from "A Vindication of the Rights of Woman" by Mary Wollstonecraft).

\begin[class=book, papersize=129mm x 198mm]{document}
\define[command=em]{\font[family="Garamond Premier Pro",style=italic,
features=+swsh:+dlig:+hlig]{\process}}
% requirement packages
\define[command=smcp]{\font[family="Garamond Premier Pro",features=+smcp]{\process}}

How grossly do they insult us, who thus advise us only to render
ourselves gentle, domestic brutes!  For instance, the winning
softness, so warmly, and frequently recommended, that governs by
obeying.  What childish expressions, and how insignificant is the
being\mdash{}can it be an immortal one?  who will condescend to govern by
such sinister methods! \em{\ldquo{}Certainly,\rdquo{}} says Lord Bacon, \em{\ldquo{}man is of
kin to the beasts by his body: and if he be not of kin to God by
his spirit, he is a base and ignoble creature!\rdquo{}}  Men, indeed,
appear to me to act in a very unphilosophical manner, when they try
to secure the good conduct of women by attempting to keep them
always in a state of childhood.  Rousseau was more consistent when
he wished to stop the progress of reason in both sexes; for if men
eat of the tree of knowledge, women will come in for a taste:  but,
from the imperfect cultivation which their understandings now
receive, they only attain a knowledge of evil.

\end{document}

issue.title: Allow to configure implicitly required variables for JSX identifiers via pluggable API

comment.body:
I was able to achieve the two goals using the existing rules extension behaviours, and have submitted them as PRs to https://github.com/yannickcr/eslint-plugin-react

1. **Ensure that `React` is in scope whenever JSX is used**
    https://github.com/yannickcr/eslint-plugin-react/issues/5
    This one is fairly straightforward, for every opening JSX tag, use the same algorithm as `no-undef` to make sure `React` is available.
2. **Count JSX towards use of the `React` variable**
    https://github.com/yannickcr/eslint-plugin-react/issues/6
    This one is a bit trickier, because it needs to silence some false-positives from `no-unused-vars`. The current approach I took was to take advantage of the internal implementation of the unused vars check, and have this new rule annotate the appropriate `React` variable whenever a JSX tag is opened. The tradeoffs of this approach are discussed in the linked PR.

These two checks should achieve the desired effect of changes suggested in this issue.

https://gist.github.com/sootysax/14b0f768c0e7e8797f75/
log: driving forward through silage area with debug 1 active

CP Version 0064
Holzhausen15 Map
Using a Deutz 6.61 with a Euroboss 330 forage wagon. 

Generated course will fill wagon to 100% and tractor will proceed to the unloading route, but beacon will not come on.  'Drive now' button is still visible.

Reaching the silage area, the tractor will drive straight through and not unload and return to the field.
Tip Trigger reached is displayed and the unload icon lights up.  This is driving forward thru the dump area.

If I stop and restart the course on the unload section and hit the 'drive now' button, the trailer will unload 5% of the load and then drive through without unloading the rest.

If I record a course that reverses into the silage area, the tractor will start dumping at the back of the pit and pull forward and reverse again, back and forth, dumping in sections 2&3 and then pulling out, leaving the wagon 28% full.

https://gist.github.com/sootysax/3861de344be005afaec2/
log: reverse with debug 1 

ALSO:

CP does not seem to realize that the wagon is full..   If, on the way to the last waypoint to start the unload route, the tractor gets hung up on a tree or a fence, and you have to resume the course from the nearest waypoint, the trailer will proceed along the fieldwork course and not to the unload route even though the wagon is at 100%.   Hitting the Drive Now button has no effect.   The only way to get the tractor to proceed to the unload route is to cancel and reload a saved route.   

I think this is the reason that it is not unloading at the silage area, it doesn't realize it is on the unload route.

issue.title: [WIP] Gaussian process revisited

milestone.description:
This milestone is not really associated with a deadline.
I intend it as a list of things we think have to be done before we get there.

issue.body:
This PR intents to address some of the points on the wish list for Gaussian processes that have been discussed on the mailing list recently.  Among the features are
 * kernel engineering (combining basic kernels using "+" and "*" operators)
 * gradient-based hyperparameter optimization
 * estimating the global noise level as part of the hyperparameter optimization (using a "WhiteKernel")
 * Gaussian process classification
 * sampling of functions from GP prior and GP posterior

Examples for this PR are (for the moment) in examples/gaussian_process/new. 

This PR deliberately avoids any interdependency with the existing GP code and starts completely from scratch. This is surely debatable but in my opinion the interface of the existing GP is part of the problem as it separates the specification of the kernel and its parameters which makes more complex kernels close to impossible to specify. Moreover, the existing code is not amenable for extensions, in my opinion. 

This PR is still in an early state with several open issues and incomplete documentation. Feedback is very welcome. There are definitely some open questions left in this PR, in particular:
 * how could we make a transition from the "old" GP code to the new one? Do we want to do that or should this code live rather as an extension module outside of sklearn? So far, I haven't removed any of the old code.
 * clarify the details of specifying advanced kernels, in particular the lower and upper boundary for the hyperparameters. If someone has an alternative idea to the current triple-based notation (preliminary documentation of this in kernel.py), I am very open for changing it.

List of todos:
  - [ ] explicit basis function for GPR (GPML book, chapter 2.7)
  - [ ] support multiple restarts of gradient-based optimization
  - [ ] optimize all hyperparameters with specified search-space, keep other hyperparameters fixed (currently only all or none is supported) 
  - [ ] replace deepcopy(kernel) by kernel_with_params()
  - [x] test kernels for stationarity
  - [ ] implement special method `__eq__` for GPs
  - [ ] check dimensionality of returned value of GPC.predict_proba()
  - [ ] test GP kernels with kernel regression
  - [ ] deprecate legacy GP code (GaussianProcess, correlation_models, regression_models)
  - [ ] adapt legacy tests/examples if possible; remove otherwise 
  - [ ] move CO2 data to mldata
  - [ ] complete documentation

Some plots:
GP classification
![gpc](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1116263/6274705/bde22c48-b879-11e4-9522-dfce288ccba8.png)

Estimation of noise-level:
![noise-estimation](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1116263/6274724/d4dc711a-b879-11e4-9582-43eaaa3dfed2.png)

Illustration of GP prior and GP posterior based on sample-function:
![prior_posterior](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/1116263/6274736/eb01f2b2-b879-11e4-9b68-4976be198cd7.png)

comment.body:
> That plot is beautiful! :) Where do you see the bottleneck that can be optimized with cython? I didn't see anything immediately while scanning over what you added for this example.

I should have done the profiling first; the major bottleneck was in an unexpected part (as always), namely in the computation of the gradient in log_marginal_likelihood() and not in the kernel code. By using einsum rather than trace(dot(...)), this should run now a lot faster.

issue.title: Downloading  File Causes "A Task was canceled" Exception
issue.body:
When I try to download a file about 130M in size, the sample eventually throws an exception of "A Task was canceled".

Also, both download and upload files should support cancellation and progress report. Currently, only uploading large file support progress report.

comment.body:
HttpClient will raise a TaskCanceledException if the send times out, and the default time out is 100 seconds. So, if you download a file large enough and it takes more than 100 seconds to complete, it will time out with the exception.

To support cancellation and progress report. Here is a link that may help you: https://canbilgin.wordpress.com/2012/06/17/download-send-request-asyncwithprogress-with-httpclient/

Thanks!

issue.title: Add drop-down menu for bibliographyLocale
issue.body:
Groundwork for adding a drop-down menu to the Styles tab of the Cite tab of the Zotero preferences, for selecting the bibliography locale. See also https://forums.zotero.org/discussion/45805/

Still needs some work, but I'd like some guidance on how to implement things:

 * I placed https://github.com/citation-style-language/locales/blob/master/locales.json at https://github.com/zotero/zotero/tree/4.0/resource/schema. Is that okay? How are similar files at this location being kept up to date (like "renamed-styles.json")?
 * Fresh installs of Zotero have an empty string for "extensions.zotero.export.bibliographyLocale". With the current code, an empty string value for bibliographyLocale is replaced by the value of Zotero.locale when the preference tab is loaded, or, if Zotero.locale isn't set, by "en-US". Is this behavior problematic if the pref can be set via the UI?
 * The drop-down menu options are limited to the locales for which we have CSL locale files. Should there be a way to specify a custom locale code for "extensions.zotero.export.bibliographyLocale" via the UI? If so, what should that look like? A "Custom..." entry at the bottom of the drop-down list, that, if selected, pops up a dialog box with a text box?
 * Should there be a top-five list of most-recently used locales at the top of the drop-down list?
 * For some reason the drop-down box stretches across the entire window. Not sure why. XUL beats me.
 * I removed `width` on `<label id="export-citePaperJournalArticleURL" width="45em">`, since it didn't do anything on OS X. Is this still necessary? Maybe we can check on other platforms.

comment.body:
Do people agree that it might be preferable to not save the "export.lastStyle" pref when selecting a style with a default-locale (for those cases where the locale menulist responds to the selected style: Export Bibliography, Doc Prefs, RTF Scan)? That would give the user a bit more flexibility.

E.g. if "export.lastStyle" is "fr-FR", and the user exports a bib in Nature format (default-locale="en-GB"), the output will be in "en-GB". If the user then exports a bib again with APA, it will default to "fr-FR". I think that's more desirable than switching "export.lastStyle" to "en-GB" in this case.

issue.title: ADT support
issue.body:
This looks similar but it ends up treating enums specially.
Personally I like ADTs better, more generic but this'll probably cover 90% of use cases too.

Here's something I'd try:

Product type: implicit, existing 'fields' construct takes care of that,
fields": [
                { "name": "base", "type": "action_event_base" },
                { "name": "look_id", "type": "long" },
...............
]
That effectively is a type constructor that requires a union of all fields.
Even 'required' stuff is fine, we represent it as an optional type, so it doesn't break type sig.

So, the missing part is the 'sum' type, to support it I'd try something like

"foo": {
  description: ...
  fields: [....]
}

"bar": {
  description: ....
  fields: [....]
}

foos: {
  description: ....
  sum: [ "foo", "bar" ]
}


-------------------
Now, imagine we are taking care of the simplest possible case (foo and bar are just 'constants', have no fields as such.
All we need to do to support that is to make 'fields' part optional.

E.g. Sean's example might look like:

"RECEIPT": {
  "description": "Used when an inventory adjustment is related to receipt of inventory"
},
"ADJUSTMENT": {
  "description": "Used when inventory is incremented/decremented for some reason, for example indicating Lost/Found inventory"
 },
.......................

event_type: {
  description: ...........
  sum: [ "RECEIPT", "ADJUSTMENT" ]
}

Scala equivalent:

sealed trait EventType

case object Receipt extends EventType
case object Adjustment extends EventType

object EventType {
   def all: Seq[EventType] ....
  ... other convenience methods we've discussed for this pattern (and IIRC mreed already implemented elsewhere)
}

Corresponding Haskell code would be:)

data EventType = Receipt | Adjustment

One other small but practical issue here is name spaces.
This is not only tied to enums but perhaps we might run into it faster trying to define enums, their names tend to be shorter, conflict is more likely.
Currently everything is globally scoped in a particular api.json.
Maybe for 'microservice' architecture it's fine, scopes will be small.
OTOH maybe we want to follow what's been done elsewhere and figure out scoping rules, so that you can have 'RECEIPT' and 'ADJUSTEMENT' types in different 'enums' in a different context.
Remember when we talked about it a while ago I compared this to ORM frameworks? :) This is one of them corner cases that may affect design. I'm sure there's many more.
Overall this is a rather nuanced problem, overlaps a lot with programming language design.

issue.body:
Here goes.

The main entry point is the `org-journal-search` function, which asks for a search string and two dates (start end). Dates are read using the `org-read-date` function, which allows a rather free-form date entry (like `-7d` or `-1m`) plus a calendar-based date selection.

I also played with a tag-based search, which collects tags from all the files and builds an index... Don't know if it's worth it.

issue.title: Embedding API: calling function/method
issue.body:
When integrating a scripting language into a (game) engine there are chances you'll end up with an event-based approach.

On precise times, the host need to call (callback) functions and methods residing in the VM.

Currently, the only way to do this is to dynamically generate the script statement and interpret it. This is easy and versatile *but* has two major drawbacks
* the generated callback script need to be interpreted prior execution, introducing some overhead (and some events could be called a lot of times), and
* although easy, building the script statement as a string fells clumsy.

Other embedding APIs (such as NPAPI, just to name one) offer some kind of function/method calling facility. That way, no interpretation is needed (just a symbol look-up and execution) and the programmer will surely feel smarter in using a well-defined API rather than hacking the callback into the VM.

I guess this can be done both for functions and class methods (static symbols) and instance methods (dynamic symbols). For the latter, I guess the instance variable name (or pointer?) should be passed, but that won't be an issue.

These are some random thoughts I wrote for you to comment. The surely need to be refined, but might be a starting point for a discussion.

comment.body:
> I really like your choice in using a variable-argument-list to pass the actual parameters to the mathod call (the other option being an open array of some customary "variant" type). Sleek.

Yeah, I think doing a variant in C-land would add a lot of complexity and overhead for wrapping.

> It enables the very same WrenMethod variable to be called different times with different values/types (if needed and/or make sense).

Yup, that's what I had in mind. :) It does feel a bit redundant to pass the signature into `wrenGetMethod()` and then pass the argument type string to `wrenCall()`. I'm considering trying to unify those, so you'd do:

```c
WrenMethod* method = wrenGetMethod(vm, "module", "variable", "someMethod(s,b,i)");
wrenCall(method, "str", true, 123);
```

And that would give you a method handle both to some typed argument list. If you wanted to call the same method with different argument types, you could just get multiple handles to the same method with different arg types.

But, now that I think about it, this will add a decent amount of complexity to the implementation, so it's probably not worth doing. There is something nice about having the "format string" right next to the argument list. Makes it easier to keep them in sync.

> (in fact I'm needing this feature in the engine I'm developing)

I have a little not-even-a-toy game engine that also needed this. :)

> By the way, I also have in plan to do a regression test to check whether the MSVC build is still "warning-free" following the generous recent changes/additions.

Sounds good, thanks! Travis is at least doing the C++ build now, so that should flush out some of these errors.

issue.title: Register Phone - Daemon Mode
issue.body:
I managed to make the daemon version work perfectly.
But how do I register the phone?
I tried after the telnet connection and enter the phone did not work .
I tried to also put in the configuration the option -u user 5591xxxxxxxx and did not work well. How should I do?

comment.body:
Ok guy's

In short you need the /home/<user>/.telegram-cli/<files> So a user without no homedir does not work. It has no credentials or verification to write/read.

Sollution:

1) create a user with homedir.
2) Run telegram-cli under this user once to register.
3) Run the daemon as this user.

issue.title: Ruby Client Hard to Follow
issue.body:
TBH, I found the ruby client very hard to follow.  (For reference, I was using the client generated by transactional email service https://gist.github.com/jenglert/3539880a906da1cd1357).  Basically, we need to make it easier to figure out how to use the thing.  Some suggestions:

* It would greatly aid readability if the actual bits you might call were at the top of the file.
* Classes that are repeated in every client should be at the bottom, and hopefully below a comment indicating that stuff below the comment isn't client specific (and can be ignored by people looking for the interface).
* The models module should come after the clients module
* My method to send email was named 'post'.  This isn't really great in my opinion.  The method should be named sendMail IMO.  Consider someone reading an application of the client.  It would be much easier to parse
```
client.messages.sendMail(...)
```
rather than
```
client.messages.post(...)
```
* The method post accepted a hash instead of a list of parameters.  This makes it hard to know which information you need to pass in the Hash to get an email to send.  It also makes it hard to type check anything other than the fact that I supplied a hash.  For example, the following should have provided a more concrete error message:
```
>> client.messages.post({})
TransactionalEmailDeliveryService::HttpClient::ServerError: TransactionalEmailDeliveryService::HttpClient::ServerError
	from (irb):235:in `http_request'
	from (irb):204:in `do_request'
	from (irb):158:in `post'
	from (irb):81:in `post'
	from (irb):467
	from :0
```
* Error messages are fairly undecipherable.  For example, I have no idea why this is failing.  I think we should consider error messaging a first class product of the client.
```
>> client.messages.post({"idempotent_token"=>"test", "subject"=>"hi", "body"=>"body", "to"=>"englert.james@gmail.com", "account"=> "gilt", "email_description"=>"jimtest", "priority"=>1})
TransactionalEmailDeliveryService::HttpClient::ServerError: TransactionalEmailDeliveryService::HttpClient::ServerError
	from (irb):235:in `http_request'
	from (irb):204:in `do_request'
	from (irb):158:in `post'
	from (irb):81:in `post'
	from (irb):477
	from :0
```

issue.title: Properly configure WinRM for bootstrapping; Fixes #203
issue.body:
This change ensures WinRM is configured to allow the initial chef-client  run (CCR) to succeed. The following changes are applied to the base WinRM config:

* Increase WinRM’s max timeout to __30 minutes__ (from a default of 60 seconds).
* Increase the maximum memory allowed per WinRM session to __600MB__ (from a default of 150MB).

These configuration changes will _ONLY_ be applied if the bootstrap protocol is set to `winrm`.

/cc @adamedx

comment.body:
Thanks @schisamo! Can you make this behavior part of a new option in the create command, rather than the default behavior?  Here's why:

1. The unattend xml may be used in other use cases or parts of Azure infrastructure to customize the VM. For example, the guest agent customizations may be installed this way, and specifying our own xml may override those customizations. I'm going to validate that with this pr the guest agent process is still running (e.g. `(Get-Service WindowsAzureGuestAgent).status -eq System.ServiceProcess.ServiceControllerStatus]::Running`)
2. This is modifying default configuration of stock images -- I think such modifications should be opt-in to the degree that it is possible. And some organizations may be caught by surprise a the deviation from default config if we don't make them aware in some way -- this could trigger audit alarms in tightly managed use cases for instance.

Once we've had it out in the world for a while with enough time to add coverage for different scenarios, we can look at moving this to the default (in which case we'd address issue 2 by allowing an option to disable it).

@schisamo, can you also open an issue for us to update the README with examples of the new option once you have that?

Thank you!

issue.title: Ruby Client Hard to Follow
issue.body:
TBH, I found the ruby client very hard to follow.  (For reference, I was using the client generated by transactional email service https://gist.github.com/jenglert/3539880a906da1cd1357).  Basically, we need to make it easier to figure out how to use the thing.  Some suggestions:

* It would greatly aid readability if the actual bits you might call were at the top of the file.
* Classes that are repeated in every client should be at the bottom, and hopefully below a comment indicating that stuff below the comment isn't client specific (and can be ignored by people looking for the interface).
* The models module should come after the clients module
* My method to send email was named 'post'.  This isn't really great in my opinion.  The method should be named sendMail IMO.  Consider someone reading an application of the client.  It would be much easier to parse
```
client.messages.sendMail(...)
```
rather than
```
client.messages.post(...)
```
* The method post accepted a hash instead of a list of parameters.  This makes it hard to know which information you need to pass in the Hash to get an email to send.  It also makes it hard to type check anything other than the fact that I supplied a hash.  For example, the following should have provided a more concrete error message:
```
>> client.messages.post({})
TransactionalEmailDeliveryService::HttpClient::ServerError: TransactionalEmailDeliveryService::HttpClient::ServerError
	from (irb):235:in `http_request'
	from (irb):204:in `do_request'
	from (irb):158:in `post'
	from (irb):81:in `post'
	from (irb):467
	from :0
```
* Error messages are fairly undecipherable.  For example, I have no idea why this is failing.  I think we should consider error messaging a first class product of the client.
```
>> client.messages.post({"idempotent_token"=>"test", "subject"=>"hi", "body"=>"body", "to"=>"englert.james@gmail.com", "account"=> "gilt", "email_description"=>"jimtest", "priority"=>1})
TransactionalEmailDeliveryService::HttpClient::ServerError: TransactionalEmailDeliveryService::HttpClient::ServerError
	from (irb):235:in `http_request'
	from (irb):204:in `do_request'
	from (irb):158:in `post'
	from (irb):81:in `post'
	from (irb):477
	from :0
```

issue.title: Collection, Template, Item and Query iterable ceorcision and type checking
issue.body:
Ricardo,

I'd like to discuss the following changes to the interface and see if it is worthwhile.

A colleague of mine hit an issue. It was something along the following lines:

```
n = 10
col = Collection('href')
col.items = [Item() for i in range(n)]
col.to_dict()   # throws an attribute error
```

What is going on is that he unknowingly changed the items attribute from an *Array* to a *list*, which causes it to break later on the call to to_dict(). This may be a case of buyer beware, but I thought it would be nice to either make those attributes read-only or enforce the same assignment semantics as on construction. I implemented the latter in this pull request.

As a result you can now do the above and the list will be converted to an Array. Additionally, for those attributes which are sub-elements I also check to ensure they are either None, a dictionary or the type they are intended. Any other result throws a TypeError.

Please look it over when you get a chance -- and let me know what you think.

Dan

issue.title: Non-strict parsing mode in the newest version?
issue.body: You have written a great library, thank you so much! Your code in version 4 looks really clean, I am impressed. It seems that now the JSON parser only operates in what you were calling strict-mode in your previous version. Now if the JSON is not well formed it returns an error instead of parsing in a non-strict manor. Would you consider replacing the original non-strict parsing behavior? Perhaps that would ruin the cleanliness of your new code and it is not reasonable to expect a JSON parser to handle ill formed strings, but I did think it was really nice when your previous code gracefully accepted what now it simply rejects. Previously it seemed that strings inside the JSON did not necessarily need quotation marks, and tokens could be separated with spaces as well as commas. Perhaps even more was allowed through the old non-strict parser that other more strict parsers would reject. I am using your library to parse JSON that I type on a command line and your previous non-strict version saved me from having to type lots of characters that I now need to add. Perhaps I am being lazy and sloppy, but would you please consider restoring the old behavior, at least as an option?

pull_request.title: Adds support for Continous Integration
pull_request.body:
I've been wanting to pull this one out for a while, and finally I did it.
This PR adds continuous integration for the Elixir Website,
It runs two different kinds of validation,

**html5validator**
[The W3C Validator](http://validator.w3.org/) developed by W3C and Mozilla.
It uses a precompiled package for python ([html5validator](https://github.com/svenkreiss/html5validator)).
This is the de-facto validator for html5, it will only check the markup validity

**html-proof**
[html-proof](https://github.com/gjtorikian/html-proofer) is a Ruby Gem. It will do all kind of validations, in addition to validate markup, it will check for favicons, external scripts being loaded, broken links and also internal broken links, images (internal and external). Anything that can break overtime (specially because we rely on external sources, ie, images, fonts, libraries), this will check for that, every time we make a commit.

The reality is that our website was not passing neither of both validations due to bugs [[1](https://github.com/svenkreiss/html5validator/issues/4),[2](https://github.com/gjtorikian/html-proofer/issues/190),[3](https://github.com/gjtorikian/html-proofer/issues/191)]  in these validators, and due nature of the website having hacky code to fix issues with old browsers. So that's why i created a script that will filter the errors in STDERR, and let us run the validators in Travis.

I wish we could [validate the css code](http://jigsaw.w3.org/css-validator/), but right now it's not possible, because the css it too hacky to support IE6 i think.

Links to the elixir documentation within the website have been disabled, because the /docs/ folder it not hosted within this project, We could configure html-proof to rewrite those relative links to absolute, but right now [a bug](https://github.com/gjtorikian/html-proofer/issues/192) prevented me from doing so. Anyway, I ran it locally, and I know it's all good.

You can see the travis build here: Usually it's been taking 1m 45sec, 
https://travis-ci.org/eksperimental/elixir-lang.github.com

2. Also adds KML and KMZ support to `viewerDragDropMixin` and the Cesium Viewer app `source` parameter.

No matter what, it will be private for 1.7 since we still need to figure out the exact details of height reference support.  This is more about laying ground work.

Also, just a reminder that you'll want to either set `InfoBoxViewModel.defaultSanitizer` to `undefined` or comment out line 161 of `InfoBoxViewModel` when you're playing with this in order to avoid balloon descriptions getting neutered. I plan on addressing this in an unrelated pull (hopefully before 1.7).  You'll also want to use the proxy if you play with public Network Links.

vt(4): Add support to "downgrade" from eg. vt_fb to vt_vga

The main purpose of this feature is to be able to unload a KMS driver.

When going back from the current vt(4) backend to the previous backend,
the previous backend is reinitialized with the special VDF_DOWNGRADE
flag set. Then the current driver is terminated with the new "vd_fini"
callback.

In the case of vt_fb and vt_vga, this allows the former to pass the
vgapci device vt_fb used to vt_vga so the device can be rePOSTed.

Fix broken encapsulation of modules in io.js
issue.body:
Currently module loader looks for `node_modules` directory upwards recursively until the root of the file system is reached. This feature breaks module encapsulation as its dependencies can be pulled from global folder `/node_modules`.

The docs on `modules` say:
>For example, if the file at '/home/ry/projects/foo.js' called require('bar.js'), then io.js would look in the following locations, in this order:
/home/ry/projects/node_modules/bar.js
/home/ry/node_modules/bar.js
/home/node_modules/bar.js
/node_modules/bar.js
This allows programs to localize their dependencies, so that they do not clash.

The second feature is that we can require specific files from the module.

The docs says:

>You can require specific files or sub modules distributed with a module by including a path suffix after the module name. For instance require('example-module/path/to/file') would resolve path/to/file relative to where example-module is located.

This also breaks the module encapsulation as we can require everything, not just the functionality a module wanted to export.

Won't it be wise to deprecate these 2 features and finally drop them in io.js v2.0.0?

P.S.: I also haven't seen that those features were used in any popular project.

comment.body:
@cjihrig Thanks, I'm quite acquainted with the docs. 

I've always thought that those concepts of API locks were inspired by the fact that Joyent was unable reach the node.js v1.0.0 milestone and resulting businesses concerns about API instability. So there was a need to lock certain most crucial parts of the API to finally release something stable. 

Now when io.js managed to release version 1.0 and embraced semantic versioning the model should change. All APIs of io.js v1.0.0 should remain intact for all 1.* releases disregarding of their assigned 'stability index'. But at the same time any breaking change can be scheduled for v2.0.0 if only this change is for the better.

So what I actually expected opening this issue was not to push the breaking change to 1.* branches but to have a discussion of how `module` in io.js can be improved in the future if only this future exists for API with stability index 3.

Overhaul savegame format and loading
issue.body:
The savegame mechanism is currently quite complicated and error-prone. Just see the discussions in #376, #179, #186, and #354. The current level savegame system works like this:

* Saving
  * Each loaded level’s name is saved into the save file (think sublevels)
  * For each level, all _spawned_ objects are saved completely into the savegame, i.e. with all information required to recreate the `cSprite` subclass instance.
  * For each level, diffs are saved for the regular level objects, i.e. those have _not_ been spawned, but loaded from the level XML. The diff contains the difference in attributes between the original version in the level XML and the current version in the played game state.
* Loading
  * The XML file for the level itself is loaded for each level
  * All spawned objects are loaded by creating entirely new instances of the `cSprite` classes, which are then added to each level
  * All objects in each level are iterated. If the initial (X|Y) position of the object as encountered here matches the initial (X|Y) position of an object diff in the savegame, the diff is applied to the object (i.e. its attributes are changed accordingly).

The last step in the loading process is a mess, because the position match fails way to often. Also, handling spawned objects and regular objects differently results in lots of code duplication. There are two entirely separate hierarchies for loading objects, the `Load_From_Savegame()` virtual method hierarchy of `cSprite` and subclasses for only loading the diffs, and the `XmlAttributes` constructors of `cSprite` and subclasses, which are used to construct the spawned objects.

To remove all the code duplication, I suggest to unify the handling of spawned objects and regular objects so that all savegame loading always uses the `XmlAttributes` constructor and `Load_From_Savegame()` is removed completely. There’s no need to have two loading hierarchies with duplicate code. This requires that the regular objects are saved into the savegame XML with the same amount of information as the spawned objects, which is a **savegame format change** and hence breaks backward compatibility. The advantages are clear: No more code duplication, and even better, the hacky position checking goes away, because all objects are saved in their current state in the XML file.

We’ll have to discuss whether we want the static sprites to also save into the savegame XML. That would allow to load a savegame completely independant from the level file, so that there’s no fear that in an old savegame you suddenly saved over an abyss that was placed there in a newer version of the level.

Valete,
Quintus

comment.body:
This save and reload system drives me mad. The constructors for objects saved in level XML do not cascade, but instead to some weird mix of their own `Init()` and a different parent class constructor.

I have arrived at a point where I would immediately rewrite the entire saving system from scratch and throw everything over board. Only backward compatibility blocks this, as it always does. The saving/loading code is crap, seriously. Making newer approaches work with the old format creates even more crappy code.

Valete,
Quintus

issue.body:
(This is linked to #13.)

A game implementation should be able to provide the following information for each cell:
- its fate (one of "stay dead" or "birth" for currently dead cells, and "survive", "death by isolation" and "death by overcrowding" for currently live ones
- its age, i.e. how many generations the cell has been dead or alive

Because computing and tracking these properties is not free, also add "light" implementations that don't compute them.

issue.title: New visualization mode
issue.body:
Right now the view of the cells is pretty basic: all live cells are represented by the same character (*). Cells born in the current generation are drawn in green, others in white.

Here's a more fancy visualization mode:
- use different characters according to the "fate" of the cell: will it die of isolation, overcrowding, or will it survive?
- use different colors according to the age of the cell: e.g. different colors for cells born 0, 1, 2, 5+, 10+ generations ago

This requires changes in the game implementations to compute and keep track of these new informations (fates and ages).

```

receiving a message

mission briefing

issue.title: R.propOr not as useful as lodash's _.result; should it throw if object is undefined?

comment.body:
`R.propOr` is not, in my view, well suited to pipelining. As an example, let us get the list of strings from a data structure we *hope* will have the form:

```javascript
{a: {b: {c: ['foo', 'bar', 'baz']}}}
```

As a starting point, consider the imperative solution:

```javascript
o.a == null ? [] : o.a.b == null ? [] : o.a.b.c == null ? [] : o.a.b.c
```

Here's a possible Ramda solution:

```javascript
R.pipe(R.propOr({}, 'a'),
       R.propOr({}, 'b'),
       R.propOr([], 'c'))
```

The `R.propOr` solution is okay, but it does complect each step with the step following: in the first and second steps we provide a safe intermediate value to prevent the next step from throwing.

[Sanctuary][1] tackles this issue head-on:

```javascript
R.pipe(S.get('a'),
       R.chain(S.get('b')),
       R.chain(S.get('c')),
       S.fromMaybe([]))
```

By acknowledging that certain computations may fail, Sanctuary makes it possible to compose "unsafe" functions. Assume that the uncertain data structure above is actually sent as JSON in a request body, so we must parse the JSON string before performing the property lookups.

Possible Ramda solution:

```javascript
R.pipe(function(body) {
         try {
           return JSON.parse(body);
         } catch (err) {
           return {};
         }
       },
       R.propOr({}, 'a'),
       R.propOr({}, 'b'),
       R.propOr([], 'c'))
```

Since Ramda does not acknowledge that operations may fail, it's necessary for the parse function to return a safe intermediate value.

Here's the equivalent Sanctuary code:

```javascript
R.pipe(S.parseJson,  // sugar for S.encase(JSON.parse)
       R.chain(S.get('a')),
       R.chain(S.get('b')),
       R.chain(S.get('c')),
       S.fromMaybe([]))
```

I've found Ramda + Sanctuary to be a wonderful pairing. :)


[1]: https://github.com/plaid/sanctuary

issue.title: Optional maps now default to Map.empty instead of none in Client
issue.body:
This is caused by a change in the apidoc generated client, which provides an empty map as default for the "routing" field of an alert.
When customer enables/disables an alert, the www component issues a PATCH, passing just the "enabled" field, with a value of true/false, as specified by the selection. However, the new apidoc client turns this into a PATCH that carries both the "enabled" field and the "routing" field, with an empty map value. In turn, the API interprets this as a request to set the "enabled" field to the given boolean value, but also to reset the "routing" field of the alert.
One workaround would be for the www component to re-submit the "routing" field of the alert along with the "enabled" value. A proper fix would require changing the apidoc generated client to use Option[Map] for the optional routing map of the alert, with a default value of None. This is how apidoc used to be a while back.

pull_request.title: [Discussion] Demonstrate failing test for camel <> underscore conversion
pull_request.body:
These tests do not agree: [underscore to camel conversion](https://github.com/jpvanhal/inflection/blob/master/test_inflection.py#L317-L318) and [camel to underscore conversion](https://github.com/jpvanhal/inflection/blob/master/test_inflection.py#L332-L333)

If I'm reading correctly they use the same data and changing area51_controller Iike I did should cause two tests to fail but only one test fails. This means that words with numbers can only be converted one way: `address_1` will go `address1` but `address1` will not go back to `address_1`. I suggest using numbers as boundaries so that Area51Controller becomes area_51_controller. Thoughts?

Related issue https://github.com/ngenworks/rest_framework_ember/issues/22

pull_request.title: [Discussion PR] Complete refactor of Pathfinder
pull_request.body:
The whole intent of this pull request is basically to review and discuss the changes I introduced in the pathfinder architecture and algorithm, find better solutions and guide the development to a better version. According to unit test benchmarks and some playtests I've thrown in, I've achieved approximately a 20% increased performance in the pathfinder. However, I need some help in order to implement integration tests to make some real and better pathfinding benchmarking as it seems quite complex to create Map, Actor and World instances and I'm not fully aware of how it works.

If someone wants to test in-game differences between legacy pathfinder and the new pathfinder, he or she should simply go to the file OpenRA.Mods.Common\Traits\World\Pathfinder\PathFinderInfo.cs and change the line "return new PathFinderCacheDecorator(new PathFinder(init.World), new PathCacheStorage(init.World));" to "return new PathFinderCacheDecorator(new LegacyPathFinder(init.World), new PathCacheStorage(init.World));". This is one of the advantages of the changes I introduced, it's rather easy to switch implementation strategies.

The next steps after re-architecting the pathfinder should be to improve the A* algorithm. The 0 A.D. (another great opensource RTS game) provides some interesting documentation and strategies they use for their pathfinder: https://github.com/0ad/0ad/blob/master/docs/pathfinder.tex

I made a complete refactor of the Pathfinder trait, based upon PR #7358. The goals of these changes are:

- Isolate the dependencies (by extracting interfaces of classes like
  Actor, Map and World) of the pathfinder trait and A* algorithm and
  allow testability

- Follow software engineering design patterns and best practices (SOLID
  design principles) to create smaller, focused and isolated classes and
  methods to allow to easily swap, create and benchmark different implementations
  (through dependency injection), extend functionality and follow the SRP
  principle and, of course, easier to read and understand.

- Detect redundant calculations and unfitted data structures for several
  problems

- Ultimately, performance improvements

In detail, the changes introduced in this commit are the following:

- The changes in PR #7358 (fragmented methods from the Expand algorithm,
  fragmented the caching capabilities from the PathFinder class,
  introduced interfaces to Actor, Map, and World classes, enabled unit
  testability.

- Fragmented the whole code which regards to pathfinding into several
  files, placed inside its own folder "Pathfinder".

- Improved the path cache (PathCacheStorage class) to work with a
  Dictionary structure instead of a list for faster lookups and removals

- Modified the CellLayer class to work with the Prototype design pattern,
  and encapsulated this functionality in the class instead of making the
  PathSearch class responsible for it.

- Code which lookup up for "PathFinder" trait now looks for the
  "IPathFinder" trait.

- Extracted interface in the PriorityQueue class to be able to work with
  both the former implementation or with a .Net SortedSet data structure.
  Using one implementation or the other should be dependant on benchmarks
  and use cases (Insertions in SorterSet are O(log n), removals and
  Min lookups are O(1) while insertions in PriorityQueue are O(1) but Pops
  are O(n log n)).

- Extracted interface for the PathSearch class so we can provide different
  implementations for the A* algorithm. 2 implementations for PathSearch
  and Pathfinder are provided
  currently: LegacyPathFinder and LegacyPathSearch (which contains the
  same implementation as the former PathSearch class, only adapted to work
  with interfaces, which has negligible penalty cost) and PathFinder and
  PathSearch, which contains tweaked modifications of the A*, mobileinfo
  and different data structures which are better fit with their usage.
  This last implementation should be faster.

- Provided more unit tests for benchmarking.
