Refactored to simplify UserService (mostly just existing now for non-actors) and moved all the user-interaction logic into a new "UserProxy" actor.

This pattern will continue into the implementation of Rooms.
Fullheight applied to resolutions over 768px wide, links added to menu

issue.title: assert spillover from tinyformat?
issue.body:
Kurt Hornik pointed out that the `tinyformat.h` may spill assert:

>  > Where are we with textreg then? "Their" problem in assert() misuse, or do
>  > you suspect a spillover from headers (though you'd think we see that
>  > more often).
>  
>  I can only guess: grepping the old and new Rcpp sources for assert shows
>  that you now have
>  
>    /inst/include/RcppCommon.h:#include <Rcpp/utils/tinyformat.h>
>

issue.title: Prevent queue method to display output
issue.body:
I have Rollbar exception tracking enabled for my project.

I want to notify Rollbar when I have deployed a new version. This can be done with the following code:

```ruby
desc "Notifies rollbar."
task :notify_rollbar do
  revision = `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:"%H"`
  local_user = `whoami`
  rollbar_token = '???' # TODO: Store rollbar token at one single place!
  rails_env = 'production'
  queue "curl https://api.rollbar.com/api/1/deploy/ -F access_token=#{rollbar_token} -F environment=#{rails_env} -F revision=#{revision} -F local_username=#{local_user} >/dev/null 2>&1"
end
```

I then do a `invoke :'notify_rollbar'` before the `to :launch do ... end` block.

This works well, but the output from the CURL command is displayed during deployment:

```
-----> DB migrations unchanged; skipping DB migration        
-----> Skipping asset precompilation        
       % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time    Time     Time  Current
       Dload  Upload   Total   Spent    Left  Speed
109   549    0    16  106   533     21    711 --:--:-- --:--:-- --:--:--  2123    0
       { 
         "data": {} 
       }-----> Build finished 
-----> Moving build to releases/35        
-----> Updating the current symlink 
```

This is nasty. Is there a way to prevent this?

issue.title: Switch from ruby-haml to haml-coffee
issue.body:
In an effort to lower our dependencies (and make windows installation easier) I've removed all ruby-haml specific markup and converted it to coffee-haml markup.

Coffee-haml is advantageous to use b/c
1. We no longer have to install a random ruby gem
2. We could now potentially use the grunt build manager (woot, no more build dependency annoyances!)
3. The node package manager is already need for `lessc`, so it's nbd to install `haml-coffee` as well

```
The current mode is called panning. You basically grab the map like a paper on 
a desk and move it around.

page, and if you move your mouse up from this point, the page scrolls up. 
Basically you specify a vector where the map should go. It has the drawback 
that you can overshoot your target position if the scroll speed is proportional 
to the length of the vector. This mode is the inverse of the panning.

What scrolling do mean?
```

```
Now I understand what you ment. I took the decision long time ago not to 
implemet that type of scrolling. The problems:

- it is much easier to overshoot the target, then you spend 2x the time to 
correct
- game is run usually in windowed mode where there is no "infinite button" at 
the edges of the map, so no auto-scrolling

The pan based scrolling, accompanied by the wheel based scrolling lets you 
scroll more precisely as you control the distance, and not the speed-time.
```

issue.title: System.MissingMethodException during SendToAirbrake after installation of package

comment.body:
Also, our "hack" solution to get it working and verify that Airbrake was receiving errors was to un-install the SharpBrake package completely and re-install all three packages individually with the Package Manager Console (in this order):
1. Install Common.Logging.Core version 2.2.1 - (run: PM> Install-Package Common.Logging.Core -Version 2.2.1 )
2. Install Common.Logging version 2.3.1 - (run: PM> Install-Package Common.Logging -Version 2.3.1)
3. Install SharpBrake (latest version) - (run: PM> Install-Package SharpBrake)

Then we added the following to our web.config
<add key="Airbrake.ApiKey" value="[your API key]" />
<add key="Airbrake.Environment" value="[any string]" />
Note that we did NOT set a server URI key, we had to let SharpBrake use its default.

Then we added our SharpBrake using statement and a method call code to our Try/Catch block:

try
{ // some code }

catch (Exception ex)
{ 
     Extensions.SendToAirbrake(ex); 
} 

Everything worked; but we can't be certain it will continue to work over time and we can never drop everything and add SharpBrake back directly through NuGet or it will break again.

issue.title: Setup task should not be trying to chown or chmod
issue.body:
The setup task should just attempt to create the require directory structure. It is perfectly possible for the deploy user to be able to create the directories but not be permitted to run `chmod`/`chown` on them. However, if the user can create the directory structure successfully what is the need for `chmod`/`chown` to be run in the first place?

The way these commands are structure is founded on far too many assumptions. Here are the relevant lines from `mina/deploy.rb`.

```
      #{echo_cmd %{chown -R `whoami` "#{deploy_to}"}} &&
      #{echo_cmd %{chmod g+rx,u+rwx "#{deploy_to}"}} &&
```

These commands assume that:
* The deploy folder and all its subfolders must be owned by the deploying user.
* The group, which is neither defined nor managed by the setup task, must have read and execute permissions.

These assumptions are deeply flawed and I would argue that folder permissions fall well outside the purview of a deployment tool's responsibility. They should already be configured by a system provisioning tool as part of the system architecture.

For my purposes I had to clear out all of the default setup actions in order to write a sane setup script.

comment.body: I did one better; I wrote my own setup task and named it exactly the same. But I will probably not be writing a PR as I do not have the time for that and you do not seem to share my view on the limits of Mina's responsibility in deployment.

issue.title: [REQ] Multiple RDBMS support
issue.body:
Issue imported from Google Code: https://code.google.com/p/sequel-pro/issues/detail?id=362
Reporter:brandon....@gmail.com Date:2009-08-08 08:10:32 Status:Accepted

With the changes from 9.5 to 9.6, Sequel Pro is nearly flawless, and absolutely awesome.  It is by far 
my program of choice, but sometimes I have to deal with other RDBMSs, and I have to use some 
second- or third-rate tool (which is usually not free).   (I've used some tools that have more features 
than Sequel Pro, but they're usually ugly and non-intuitive, probably designed for full-time DBAs, 
not for developers.)

The name change from CocoaMySQL to Sequel Pro leaves open the possibility of supporting 
databases other than MySQL.  Of course you probably want to wait until after 1.0 to consider doing 
this, but what about supporting SQLite and PostgreSQL?    A lot of developers use SQLite locally, and 
quite a few seem to be moving to Postgres.

I realize this feature belongs on the backlog, and not something to be done right away, but please 
consider adding it.

comment.body: @dmoagx what do you think about PostgreSQL? It's pretty close to MySQL (though I don't know the bounds of the context you define closeness in terms of Sequel Pro architecture). I'd venture to guess many people would be happy to have a MySQL and PostgreSQL only Sequel Pro.

issue.title: Volume control widget cannot be displayed if only alsa-lib is installed (without libpulse)
issue.body:
If only alsa-lib is installed (and libpulse is not installed) the volume contorl widget can't be displayed.

In the Add Panel Widgets window, if I try to add the volume control widget it doesn't appear anywhere. '(1 active)' becomes temporarily written next to the volume control entry in the Add Panel Widgets window, but it disappears if I close and open that window again.

If libpulse is installed in addition (no need to install pulseaudio, just libpulse is enough), the widget appears properly. It seems that by default it is configured to use PulseAudio, so at least it appears but it doesn't have any effect, it doesn't control anything if pulseaudio isn't installed. I have to go in the Configure "Volume Control" window and select ALSA for it to work properly and control the audio.

So the workaround is to install libpulse to make the widget appear, and then to configure it to use ALSA.

The behavior that I expected from the widget is that it shouldn't want libpulse just in order to be displayed and that it should be able to be displayed with only alsa-lib. But it's not the case.

issue.title: Detached mocks (Issue 305)
issue.body: Implemented Spock Issue 305 according to https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/spockframework/pZXrWKzRV5U

comment.body:
While extracting the `MockFactory` interface and implementing the `StandaloneMockFactory` I noticed some other problems. The factory methods in `SpecInternals` all have a inferredName parameter which is unavailable in the standalone case. So we either use a fixed name based on the type or something, or require the use of the `options` map with a `name` option.

Should the initialization `Closure` be supported and if so, how should it behave? Should it be stored in the mock and executed each time it is attached to a spec? If we are not supporting them, we should throw `UnsupportedOperationException` instead of simply ignoring them.

How should the classloader be passed? It is normally taken from the spec but in the detached case I added it as parameter instead of the spec.

issue.title: Extend crossfilter plugins/chart builder concept for quick general-purpose dashboards
issue.body:
This is something I noticed after reviewing #1735. I think there is a lot of similarities behind the idea of the chart builder (added by #1735) and the crossfilter plugin (added by #1774). They are just marshalling between the user and the plot. The crossfilter plugin is marshaling between the user, the ui, and the plot.

You could think of this more generically, that the builder knows the requirements of the plot it is generating, so a more specialized builder could auto-generate a simple interactive UI for a given data source. This feature would be a step towards being able to quickly piece together multiple high level charts into a dashboard that shares the same data source. 

This would be possibly less efficient than using the low level interface for things like crossfilter, but would provide a method for more quickly building interactive dashboards.

Below is a diagram showing the concept:
![image](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/452052/6041704/860a3c98-ac44-11e4-925f-86fc19eed681.png)

comment.body:
One other thing is that specifically x and y in the FacetGroup is probably too specific. For example, if I created a Facet Tab, then it would really just be one dimensional, where the dimension is the tabs.

With crossfilter, you can combine Facet Tab with Facet Grid so that you can facet by one dimension by the tabs of plots, then facet by x and/or y in each tab. So this gives you 3 dimensions to plot plots, if that makes sense, on top of the two dimensions used for actually scattering the points. So, I'll think through how to compose the faceting operations.

> "Facets are embeddings. A facet of a facet specifies a frame embedded within a frame. A facet of a facet of a facet specifies a frame embedded within a frame embedded within a frame. Each frame is a bounded set which is assigned to its own coordinate system ... a four-dimensional graph can be realized in four 1D frames, a 1D frame embedded in a 2D frame embedded in a 1D frame, two 2D frames, a 3D frame embedded in a 1D frame, and so on."
> - Wilkinson, L. The Grammar of Graphics

issue.title: __gitmon__ directory not created during restore to 11.10.x
issue.body:
`backup_utils version 2.0.2`

The `/data/repositories/__gitmon__` directory is not being created after a restore to a 11.10 series appliance.  This has the effect of breaking the entire administration GUI **and** API.  From today's conversation with GHE support:

> ...noted that the __gitmon__ directory will not be automatically re-created yet, so you will still have to do that step manually, and I believe it will be necessary after each restore. (This issue only affects the 11.10 series; it's not needed for 2.0 or 2.1.)

The mitigation steps as provided by support are:
```bash
god stop gitmon 
yes | ghe-unlock 
sudo mkdir /data/repositories/__gitmon__ 
sudo chown -R git:git /data/repositories/__gitmon__ 
sudo enterprise-configure 
ghe-lock 
god start gitmon
```

We are being bitten by this issue across our various GHE appliances.  This is not a sustainable solution.  Can this please be highly prioritized since it's breaking restores?

Thanks!

comment.body:
I've now tested with a clean 11.10.348 instance and the same thing applies there.  The `/data/repositories/__gitmon__` directory _is_ automatically recreated.

So with the latest code in backup-utils, there is no need to run any commands manually.

issue.title: Observations
issue.body:
```
samspock@gmail.com


The mission 5 info task list says Admiral Benson and not Tulen like it should.

Building new ships have different load-outs than original. The main one I see 
is that a destroyer 1 should be built with 3 lasers but comes with none. Not a 
big deal in the later game but causes issues early in the game when money is 
tight. Also, the first ship you get does not have a hyperdrive like it does in 
the original. Not sure if that was intentional.

Using bombs and missiles do not work right either. Shooting bombs does not stop 
when you run out, it starts shooting missiles until they are gone. Same goes 
with missiles first. 

Sometimes when attacking a garthog fleet in mission 7 the fleet will run away 
before you can engage. The mission will then fail.

The game is also missing the "Research Stopped" warning when you run ot of 
money or don't have the dev centers needed to finish.

Selling ships sometimes lets you get two sales per ship and keep selling the 
last ship over and over. When I saw this I was on Captain selling my destoyer 
1's (about 10 of them). I first removed the lasers, shields and hyperdrives 
then sold the ships one at a time.
Gives lots of money :) but not what should happen.

Not sure if the bomb strength relative to the hull strenght for ground guns is 
quite right. I can take out an ion gun with 4 bombs just like the original but 
the plasma gun takes a lot more than the six required in the original, even 
assuming a few are shot down.

The mission 13 reward should be 5 lasers but it gives 16. 

I asked for reinforcements on level 2, was granted but did not get any more 
ships. 

Glad you are doing this. I bought the original in '97 and still have the 
origanl packaging and disks. One of my favorite games. Thanks.
```

```
Hi and thanks for reporting.

2) It is an issue with the startup loadout of ships, easily fixed, but will 
work on newly started games as the loadout is stored in a save. (A loadout is 
determined by the available technology once a ship is researched.)

3) Currently, it fires rockets at ships and bases, or bombs at ground 
installations with 100% damage. If you run out of these, the game switches to 
the other type with 20% damage. I remember the original game let you do the 
same. Can you double-check this?

4) AI somehow still found it's script controlled fleet and gave it another 
command. If you attacked the trader, the mission would be still playable as 
usual. Anyway, I will try to fix this.
```

issue.title: Performance degradation in 0.8.0-rc4
issue.body:
I discovered that simple app using hibernate degrades in performance from 12k req/sec to 2.2k req/sec when switching dropwizard version from 0.7.1 to 0.8.0-rc4.

Steps to reproduce:


1. `git clone git@github.com:kenota/dropwizard-perf-issue.git`
2. `cd dropwizard-perf-issue`
4. `gradle singleJar`
5. `java -jar ./build/libs/app.jar server hello-world.yml  > /dev/null`

At this point you should run some benchmark, against http://localhost:8080/video-hibernate URL. I was able to achieve 12k req/sec using 50 threads on my MacbookPro.

6. Ctrl+C to stop the running app
7. Uncomment `dropwizardVersion = "0.8.0-rc4"` line in `build.gradle` and comment out `dropwizardVersion = "0.7.1"`
8. `gradle singleJar`
9. `java -jar ./build/libs/app.jar server hello-world.yml  > /dev/null`

Run benchmark again. At this point, I was able to get only 2.2k req/sec using same 50 threads.

[Repo with code showing problem](https://github.com/kenota/dropwizard-perf-issue)

comment.body:
@arteam, thank you for suck quick reaction, especially on Saturday.  I have tried my code with 0.8.0-rc5 and can confirm that issue seems to be resolved with 0.8.0-rc5.

issue.title: MD070SD shifted row and column lines
issue.body:
Hi,
after testing the Sainsmart SSD1963 with fbtft, I got always an tearing effect with X11, so i ordered the new version of the 7" display with an MD070SD controller. The display does not need all this painful initialization code, so I just set the back light. 

sudo modprobe --first-time fbtft_device name=flexpfb debug=3 rotate=0 verbose=3  gpios=reset:2,dc:3,led:21,wr:4,db00:17,db01:27,db02:22,db03:6,db04:13,db05:19,db06:26,db07:20,db08:14,db09:15,db10:18,db11:23,db12:24,db13:25,db14:12,db15:16
sudo modprobe --first-time flexfb width=800 height=480 buswidth=16 init=-2,1,-1,0x01,16,-3

Generally the display seems to work with fbtft but I think the row lines and columns are shifted. I think this is because of the automatic line/column address calculation and increment of the controller. I tried to disable this feature, but there is no way doing this at with initialization code.

I double checked the wiring, and tested with fbtest. Photos are attached.

You can find the documentation at:
http://www.sainsmart.com/sainsmart-7-7-inch-tft-lcd-display-cpld-sdram-800x480-for-arduino-uno-mega2560.html

There is nearly the same display board with the same documentation from Iteadstudio. 
But the Sainsmart one has the additional feature to power it with 5V 500mA and 3.3V 300mA, which I think is perfect for the Pi B+ header.

http://imall.iteadstudio.com/md070sd-7-16-bit-parallel-bus-tft-module.html
ftp://imall.iteadstudio.com/TFT%20LCM/IM130820001/DS_IM130820001.pdf

What do you think about the problem, is there a way to get this working with the driver?       
Thanks in advance and for everything you've done here with this great driver!

![20150222_111002](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11144478/6318235/0fca461c-ba87-11e4-952c-5a2fa7d92b16.jpg)
![20150222_101302](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/11144478/6318236/17ac8124-ba87-11e4-9cdb-6efa16b576e2.jpg)

issue.title: WIP: Add tolerance for equality when optimizing ticks (Fix #550)
issue.body:
The main problem is in the [computation](https://github.com/dcjones/Gadfly.jl/blob/404f0aa433fa5431ba377234bd6d3427e9c174ab/src/ticks.jl#L93)

```julia
r = ceil((x_max - span) / (q*10.0^z * one_t))
```

where `z` is basically `log10(x_max - x_min)`.  If `x_max - x_min` is very small, `r` becomes too large.  Using `eps()` as the tolerance just happens to fix the failing example listed in #550, it is still too low for other examples.  For example:

```julia
y = ones(5)
y[1] = 1 + 2eps()

plot(x = 1:5, y = y, Geom.point)
```

will result in an infinite [loop](https://github.com/dcjones/Gadfly.jl/blob/404f0aa433fa5431ba377234bd6d3427e9c174ab/src/ticks.jl#L94)

@dcjones, any thoughts on how we can pick a reasonable tolerance?

comment.body: Thanks for looking into this. I wasn't able to figure out one epsilon that works, but I added another condition to preempt an infinite loop.

    ./app-simple.py

      File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/glumpy-1.0.3-py2.7-linux-x86_64.egg/glumpy/ext/__init__.py", line 6, in <module>

      File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/glumpy-1.0.3-py2.7-linux-x86_64.egg/glumpy/ext/glfw.py", line 60, in <module>

comment.body:
```
Hi

1) The messages are prioritized, it might happen that you run on very fast and 
the trade incomes just pile up before the tax income?

2) Each level costs the same as the building. I don't see any place where it 
could be printed. The short description space is too small, and the panel 
competes with the bottom-right info panel.

3) The original had a second speed level in the options. I plan to add such 
speed settings, where the base speed can be set between 1min-60min per 1 real 
second. That is, you'll experience 10 hours per second on very fast.

4) Yes, it is possible to rebuild: put tax pressure on other colonies, do the 
other missions which will give you more money. Don't demolish buildings and 
don't repair them all at once. You have to restore living conditions as soon as 
possible, e.g., repair power, housing, police. But frankly, I usually fail this 
mission in 33% of my testing. This I why I increased the reward for saving the 
traders. You can also sell radars on the other planets but then you won't be 
able to see the pirate attacks, unless you save and reload after searching...

I can't remember the original but I still think the current settings puts 
unnecessary pressure on the gamer.

The police station behaves just like in the original. On alien planets, it is 
the only source of morale boosting.

5) I set the properties of the morale in a way so that Achilles dies within 
10-12 days if unattended. Our tax is calculated by multiplying the population 
count, the tax settings and the morale. It seems the original had a different 
method. In our game, the late gameplay produces huge amount of tax whereas the 
original was somehow reduced. I think there was a factor inversely proportional 
to the number of planets you own which would increase your tax income early but 
reduce it later on, where you couldn't even spend it all.

A true test would be, given the same initial status of our game is to run 1 day 
of both without doing anything and compare the numbers. Could you do that?
```

pull_request.title: [Discussion PR] Complete refactor of Pathfinder
pull_request.body:
The whole intent of this pull request is basically to review and discuss the changes I introduced in the pathfinder architecture and algorithm, find better solutions and guide the development to a better version. According to unit test benchmarks and some playtests I've thrown in, I've achieved approximately a 20% increased performance in the pathfinder. However, I need some help in order to implement integration tests to make some real and better pathfinding benchmarking as it seems quite complex to create Map, Actor and World instances and I'm not fully aware of how it works.

If someone wants to test in-game differences between legacy pathfinder and the new pathfinder, he or she should simply go to the file OpenRA.Mods.Common\Traits\World\Pathfinder\PathFinderInfo.cs and change the line "return new PathFinderCacheDecorator(new PathFinder(init.World), new PathCacheStorage(init.World));" to "return new PathFinderCacheDecorator(new LegacyPathFinder(init.World), new PathCacheStorage(init.World));". This is one of the advantages of the changes I introduced, it's rather easy to switch implementation strategies.

The next steps after re-architecting the pathfinder should be to improve the A* algorithm. The 0 A.D. (another great opensource RTS game) provides some interesting documentation and strategies they use for their pathfinder: https://github.com/0ad/0ad/blob/master/docs/pathfinder.tex

I made a complete refactor of the Pathfinder trait, based upon PR #7358. The goals of these changes are:

- Isolate the dependencies (by extracting interfaces of classes like
  Actor, Map and World) of the pathfinder trait and A* algorithm and
  allow testability

- Follow software engineering design patterns and best practices (SOLID
  design principles) to create smaller, focused and isolated classes and
  methods to allow to easily swap, create and benchmark different implementations
  (through dependency injection), extend functionality and follow the SRP
  principle and, of course, easier to read and understand.

- Detect redundant calculations and unfitted data structures for several
  problems

- Ultimately, performance improvements

In detail, the changes introduced in this commit are the following:

- The changes in PR #7358 (fragmented methods from the Expand algorithm,
  fragmented the caching capabilities from the PathFinder class,
  introduced interfaces to Actor, Map, and World classes, enabled unit
  testability.

- Fragmented the whole code which regards to pathfinding into several
  files, placed inside its own folder "Pathfinder".

- Improved the path cache (PathCacheStorage class) to work with a
  Dictionary structure instead of a list for faster lookups and removals

- Modified the CellLayer class to work with the Prototype design pattern,
  and encapsulated this functionality in the class instead of making the
  PathSearch class responsible for it.

- Code which lookup up for "PathFinder" trait now looks for the
  "IPathFinder" trait.

- Extracted interface in the PriorityQueue class to be able to work with
  both the former implementation or with a .Net SortedSet data structure.
  Using one implementation or the other should be dependant on benchmarks
  and use cases (Insertions in SorterSet are O(log n), removals and
  Min lookups are O(1) while insertions in PriorityQueue are O(1) but Pops
  are O(n log n)).

- Extracted interface for the PathSearch class so we can provide different
  implementations for the A* algorithm. 2 implementations for PathSearch
  and Pathfinder are provided
  currently: LegacyPathFinder and LegacyPathSearch (which contains the
  same implementation as the former PathSearch class, only adapted to work
  with interfaces, which has negligible penalty cost) and PathFinder and
  PathSearch, which contains tweaked modifications of the A*, mobileinfo
  and different data structures which are better fit with their usage.
  This last implementation should be faster.

- Provided more unit tests for benchmarking.

parameter `$arrGet` has to be reset from prior call

NewsLanguage.php line 63
add `tl_news.published = 1 AND`to where clause

```
The quick research button was introduced in IG2 for convenience.

Create a similar popup panel besides the screen switcher. Structure:

QUICK RESEARCH:

- Top: current research name, progress, money, issues if any
- Middle: 4 columns for main research types, each column lists the researchable 
technologies (fully completable only?)
- Bottom: Category and subcategory, name and long description of the currently 
hovered item above. Mini image of the technology might be displayed, if the 
space usage vs. scale is acceptible?

there is a problem with the research, it should display another colored icon. 
Example: petry dish with dark green content, glowing green petri dish, red 
glowing petri dish.

Alternatively, this panel is toggle-based, so no mouse holding.

QUICK PRODUCTION:

- Gear icon, distinctive when there is actual production going on.
- Three columns for main categories
- Each cell: the product name, remaining count, a thin progress bar of the 
current progress
- When the user releases a the mouse over a cell, add 1 to larger ships, 5 to 
fighters other equipment. 
- Separator, then show the top-tier technologies in each column, e.g., Fighter 
6, Cruiser 3, Destroyer 3, etc.
- Separator, then hightlighted technology info; category, subcategory, name, 
long description, inventory level.
```

```
QUICK RESEARCH:

current progress

fighters other equipment.

6, Cruiser 3, Destroyer 3, etc.

long description, inventory level.
```

issue.title: SignalR should handle connections limit in browser
issue.body:
Currently using SignalR without websockets will prevent you from openning more then 6-7 tabs of application, since browsers have limit.

It looks like infrastructure related task to handle this limit since SignalR is responsible for selecting appropriate transport. 

Maybe it can be handled with communication between tabs, when one tab opens connection that is used by every other tab.

comment.body:
@a-h funny you should bring this up. I actually solved this problem in a similar way. There's a branch on callr dedicated to it, as well as my [tejacques/crosstab](https://github.com/tejacques/crosstab) repo.

I've actually discovered quite a bit since originally looking into this, and as @davidfowl mentioned it is very difficult to solve this problem reliably.

Here are some of the unmentioned issues that I've run into:

* Subscriptions:
  * These need to be kept track of at all times on all tabs
  * Track which channels are subscribed to overall, as well as by this particular tab. They are often different.
  * Track which hub state is sent by each particular tab.
  * When the master tab changes, the new master must subscribe to all of the events.
* IE StorageEvents trigger on the same tab. These must be ignored to conform to the spec.
* IE8 StorageEvents are not up to spec. See tejacques/crosstab#6 and [tejacques/IE8-EventListener](https://github.com/tejacques/IE8-EventListener).
* Attempting to use this on any device which runs tabs single threaded, or freezes inactive tabs will break. crosstab deals with this by user-agent sniffing devices up front to measure support, and pinging the master with a timeout in the background. This is very important because mobile is the largest growing sector of the web. If you ignore mobile it will come back to bite you. There is no easy/reliable feature detection for this that I am aware of.
* Intercepting SignalR's callbacks involves digging into the implementation specific jQuery callbacks. This is brittle and will break when SignalR removes the jQuery dependency, and might be unfixable depending on how they change it.

After going through all of these, I decided not to merge my solution with callr's master branch, because there are likely still other issues I haven't found, and using a bunch of subdomains is just too easy in comparison.

issue.title: AI: Diplomatic decisions
issue.body:
```
This is a collector issue about how the AI diplomatic reactions should be 
calculated for various negotiations and approach levels.

We have several negotiation options:

- improve relations (humble, neutral, aggresive) -> yes, maybe, no
- send money (neutral) -> yes, no
- trade agreement (neutral) -> yes, no
- surrender (neutral) -> yes, no
- declare war (neutral) -> yes, no
- ally against (neutral) -> yes, no
- ally against dargslan (neutral) -> yes, no

The problem is how to select a response.

Decision variables:

- stance to the player (0..100)
- current money
- money required to fix colony demands
- player's current observable military strength (e.g., fleets in radar, planets 
under spy satellite)
- player's current observable production potential
- discounted military strength from actual battles with the player, if any
- AI's personality ?

```

issue.title: Classes/methods for evidence-based data analytic pipelines
issue.body:
My motivation for this issue comes from the following basic problem that I encounter every day. A scientist collects data for a given question in a given subject area and wants to be able to apply the latest and best statistical approaches to analyze the data. They come to me and ask "what do I do"? I say there are 4-5 different packages that implement some version of the latest approach. In particular, each package implements a series of functions, with help pages, but perhaps not much else in guidance in how to apply each of the functions. Occasionally, there is a vignette, but not always. They say, okay but "what do I do"?

To me, the problem is we don't have a general framework for curating the best statistical methods out there to create a sound and evidence-based data analytic pipeline for common problems in many scientific areas. In my area of environmental health, we have some well-studied problems, but no established pipelines of analyzing the data from these problems. There area few areas are a bit further ahead than we are, but I think that is the exception.

Some initial thoughts on this idea can be found in this [PNAS paper](http://arxiv.org/abs/1502.03169) and in this [blog post by Jeff Leek](http://simplystatistics.org/2014/12/04/repost-a-deterministic-statistical-machine/).

The goal would be to establish 

* A way by which statistical methods could be plugged and pasted together to create an analytic pipeline
* A mechanism for benchmarking these methods (using perhaps benchmark datasets) so that better methods can be swapped in and older methods swapped out
* A report generating mechanism that shows all the analyses conducted, to allow others to see what was done and to limit selective inference
* A library of these pipelines so that users could pick and choose amongst them given the type of data/problem they have

There is obviously other software that implements some of this functionality (Galaxy comes to mind), and I think it would be good to steal what we can from them.

Okay, this obviously cannot be done in 2 days, but maybe some pieces of it could be started....

commits.message: Merge patches branch, atan2 fixes from Volker.

Fix unarchiving of symbolic functions defined at runtime without any custom methods.

Since the python_func member of function is a bitmask indicating which custom
methods are defined in Python, symbolic functions defined at runtime are
archived as regular GiNaC functions defined in C++. Unarchiving these later is
not possible, as GiNaC does not expect any other functions than those already
in the registry.

Adding a Python callback to create a new symbolic function with the given and
number of arguments if one is not found in the registry solves the unarchiving
problem while keeping the archive/pickle format the same.
Add vim swap files and ctags file to hgignore.
Use PyObject_Cmp to compare numerics wrapping Python objects.

beta() should not return numeric evaluation if both arguments are crational.

In beta_eval(), this test is used to decide if a numeric evaluation should be
returned:
    if (!ex_to<numeric>(x).is_rational() || !ex_to<numeric>(x).is_rational())

This patch fixes the typo that both tests are for the first argument x and
replaces the is_rational() test with is_crational().
Add method to ex for counting number of symbols in an expression.
The pynac C++ part of the infinities rewrite
Evaluate psi1 numerically if argument is not crational.
Added tag pynac-0.2.4 for changeset f50fb4810d97

Fix infinite loop in power::eval.

While trying to simplify exponents of Python longs, power::eval enters an
infinite loop since it doesn't expect arithmetic with crationals to produce
inexact results.

This is #13107 on Sage trac.

Do not include release version in library name. Now it is libpynac.so only.

Contributed by Julien Puydt.

Fix detection of Python.

Instructions provided by Julien Puydt.

Less verbose output during build. Use V=1 to get the verbose version.

Contributed by Julien Puydt.

Fix printing of parenthesis around exponents of power objects.

Reported and fixed by Sebastien Gouezel.

Whether parenthesis were printed or not for exponents of power objects
depended on the expression they were a part of. For example,

sage: latex(x^(2/3)+1)
x^{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)} + 1
sage: latex(x^(2/3))
x^{\frac{2}{3}}

This patch stops passing the nesting level to the print method used to
output the exponent.
Add include statements to fix building with DO_GINAC_ASSERT defined.

fixes #12 : infinite loop when normalizing an add with content in GF(2)

If the content of an add expression is in GF(2^k), normalizing this add within
a mul::eval() leads to infinite loops. The normalization is done by
multiplying by -c where c is the content. When characteristic is 2 and c is 1,
-c is also 1. So no normalization occurs, causing the eval() function to run
into this case again.

This patch introduces a check if the characteristic is 2 when setting the
normalization factor -c. In this case, the factor -1 in ZZ is used instead to
fix the sign of the leading term that is triggering the normalization in the
first place.

This was #13609 on Sage trac.

issue.title: Parse .go files for dependencies?
issue.body:
What if, instead of parsing a separate dependency file, authors could explicitly list their dependencies in the import statements? The `nut` command would parse Go files looking for vendored dependencies, and fetch / clean as necessary?

We did an experiment in an internal package and the following worked:

```go
import "github.com/user/app/_vendor/github.com/other/package@abf7t4e2"
```

We manually vendored the dependency in the app’s _vendor directory at `_vendor/github.com/other/package@abf7t4e2`. The only thing missing is a glue tool to find and fetch dependencies missing from the _vendor directory.

issue.title: Remove obsolete DLL references from mod.yaml files
issue.body:
One of the reasons for migrating all the code from `OpenRA.Mods.RA` to `OpenRA.Mods.Common` was that a mod should not depend on another mod in any way (for the official mods, at least).
But I see `mod.yaml` files containing this:
>Assemblies:
	./mods/common/OpenRA.Mods.Common.dll
	./mods/ra/OpenRA.Mods.RA.dll
	./mods/cnc/OpenRA.Mods.Cnc.dll
	./mods/d2k/OpenRA.Mods.D2k.dll

Once the migration to `Mods.Common` is complete each mod should reference only the common DLL and its own.
Putting this here so I don't forget about it as easily.

issue.title: Plot appears to hang when plotting certain vectors
issue.body:
The following code reliably hangs Gadfly:

```jl
data = repmat([sin(t/5) for t=1:100]', 10)'
S=svdfact(data) 
v=S[:V][:,1] #data matrix is of rank 1; this is the only nonsingular component
w=fill(S[:V][1,1], 10) #In exact arithmetic, equal to v
plot(x=1:10, y=w) #OK
plot(x=1:10, y=v) #Hangs
```

issue.title: Collection, Template, Item and Query iterable ceorcision and type checking
issue.body:
Ricardo,

I'd like to discuss the following changes to the interface and see if it is worthwhile.

A colleague of mine hit an issue. It was something along the following lines:

```
n = 10
col = Collection('href')
col.items = [Item() for i in range(n)]
col.to_dict()   # throws an attribute error
```

What is going on is that he unknowingly changed the items attribute from an *Array* to a *list*, which causes it to break later on the call to to_dict(). This may be a case of buyer beware, but I thought it would be nice to either make those attributes read-only or enforce the same assignment semantics as on construction. I implemented the latter in this pull request.

As a result you can now do the above and the list will be converted to an Array. Additionally, for those attributes which are sub-elements I also check to ensure they are either None, a dictionary or the type they are intended. Any other result throws a TypeError.

Please look it over when you get a chance -- and let me know what you think.

Dan

comment.body:
Ricardo,

I've addressed the issues above, documented and updated tests. Please take a look. 

1. I took the tests from your branch and expanded them slightly. I agree the array value equivalence tests unit tests are more comprehensive. IMO they are also easier to read, as they are shorter, focused and labelled better.

2. I also added TypedProperty tests for Collection.

Regarding the descriptor protocol, I think I looked at an old example, I've updated the signature to match the docs. I don't think its any less readable, I simply looked in the wrong place.

I also realized that I had a bug as I had hastily put that together as an example. In the previous example, It was being defined as a value in the class level property and that was shared by all instance of the class, so it wasn't an instance specific property (see my last two unit tests for clearer example). I changed this so that properties used the passed name as an instance level attribute name to store the data. I assumed we could store it in "_<name>". I'm not sure what I think of this, but I am open to suggestions. I also thought of adding a safety check to ensure we don't accidentally override an existing property, but I don't think its necessary.

issue.title: SPI: switch to spi-bcm2835 - what would it require?
issue.body:
Hi!

Quick question with regards to the spi drivers:

What is the reason for not switching from the spi-bcm2708 to the upstream spi-bcm2835 driver?

I wonder because I have a few improvements that I want to push upstream which might be quite helpful for a few people who are using the SPI sub-system (especially around latencies). Also I have been talking with notro to get DMA incorporated into never versions(as well as upstream) so that the TFT displays that you are starting to support do not put such a huge interrupt burden on the RPI leaving more CPU to do actual work.

The only difference I see is the LoSSI support in spi-bcm2708, which - as far as I can tell - is basically broken because there is no correct support for those 24bit/32bit reads in the first place (depending on the command sent). Actually notro (the author of the LoSSI patch for the spi-bcm2708) told me that even he is not using it with the tft drivers, because it is not really working as he assumed it would and went back to do 9x8 bit transfers instead 8x 9bit transfers.

Also from the state of the implementation I doubt that the LoSSI patches would EVER get incorporated into the upstream Linux kernel.

For things that I have lined up with the spi-bcm2835 driver please look at the wiki: https://github.com/msperl/spi-bcm2835/wiki and the corresponding  open and closed issues.
These still need to get upstream, but I am starting to work on that.

Thanks, Martin

comment.body:
Moving to upstream drivers is desired.
Submit a PR and convince us that the change won't break lots of things and we'll accept it.

Obviously the "not breaking things" is the tricky part, as it's hard to be sure exactly what people are doing with the spi-bcm2708 driver.

SPI is not something I use, so I'll have to listen to advice from the devs who use it.
Obviously you and @notro. I'd be interested in comments from @bootc who provided the original driver.

If we make a change and lots of users complain that things are broken, we'll have to revert or help the users get working again. If you are willing to help resolve issues, then that will make the switch more likely to happen.

So, if we did this, what would you expect spi users to experience after the update? What would break?

ping @pelwell for opinion.

I have an email template set up that looks like:

I have an email template set up:

    <%body%>
    Welcome to the Highlight Summary
    Heading
    -cl1-
    -cl2-
    -cl3-
    -cl4-
    -cl5-

As I understand it, that should allow for me to use -clX- as substitution values when sending email using the ruby library. I've tried many permutations of this, but nothing works.

I would like to substitute values in for the 5 different clX tags when I send the email, and nothing for the <%body%> tag. If I include the .html or .text values in the api call, it substitutes for that but not the clX fields. I’ve tried leaving the html and text values out (which gives a “Missing email body" error), making them blank (same error), and making them a single space (no error, but the email is completely empty).

How can I get these fields substituted into the template?

This is the code I’m using to send:

    recipients = {
      "Adam Fields" => "adam@XXXXXXX.com"
    }
    recipients.each{|name, email|
      mail = SendGrid::Mail.new do |m|
        m.to = email

      header = Smtpapi::Header.new

      mail.smtpapi = header

pull_request.title: Add the font package.
pull_request.body:
It provides a layer of indirection between the user and truefont.
This serves two purposes:
1. It will make it easier to replace truefont with freetype-go once the latter supports everything that we need.
2. It allows for the creation of a fake test font, for use in testing the eventual text layout code.

issue.title: Add 'appendExtension' option
issue.body:
This option allows the `.webp` extension to be appended to the path instead of replacing the original extension.

Example:

```js
gulp.src('./img/foo.{png,jpg}')
  .pipe(webp({appendExtension: true}))
  .pipe(gulp.dest('.'));
```

Creates two images: `foo.png.webp` and `foo.jpg.webp`.

issue.title: Properly configure WinRM for bootstrapping; Fixes #203
issue.body:
This change ensures WinRM is configured to allow the initial chef-client  run (CCR) to succeed. The following changes are applied to the base WinRM config:

* Increase WinRM’s max timeout to __30 minutes__ (from a default of 60 seconds).
* Increase the maximum memory allowed per WinRM session to __600MB__ (from a default of 150MB).

These configuration changes will _ONLY_ be applied if the bootstrap protocol is set to `winrm`.

/cc @adamedx

issue.title: cask install --force fails without explicit 'cask'
issue.body:
`brew install Caskroom/cask/mactex` was quit early; on repeat gave:

> Warning: A Cask for mactex is already installed. Add the "--force" option to force re-install.

So adding the `--force` option:

> `$ brew install Caskroom/cask/mactex --force`
> Warning: A Cask for mactex is already installed. Add the "--force" option to force re-install.
> `$ brew install --force Caskroom/cask/mactex`
> Warning: A Cask for mactex is already installed. Add the "--force" option to force re-install.

Figured I'd try to uninstall:

> `$ brew uninstall Caskroom/cask/mactex`
Error: No such keg: /usr/local/Cellar/mactex

Not far enough along. Only at this point did I notice from the output that `brew install Caskroom/cask` was implicitly `brew cask install`, so I tried:

> `$ brew cask install Caskroom/cask/mactex --force`

Which worked.

comment.body:
@mikemcquaid From my perspective, I'd suggest an 'all or nothing' approach.

If it had failed at `brew install Caskroom/...` I would have presumably identified the issue much sooner (first time using `brew cask`), and never would have made the mistake with `--force` and associated cryptic error.

issue.title: Fix broken encapsulation of modules in io.js
issue.body:
Currently module loader looks for `node_modules` directory upwards recursively until the root of the file system is reached. This feature breaks module encapsulation as its dependencies can be pulled from global folder `/node_modules`.

The docs on `modules` say:
>For example, if the file at '/home/ry/projects/foo.js' called require('bar.js'), then io.js would look in the following locations, in this order:
/home/ry/projects/node_modules/bar.js
/home/ry/node_modules/bar.js
/home/node_modules/bar.js
/node_modules/bar.js
This allows programs to localize their dependencies, so that they do not clash.

The second feature is that we can require specific files from the module.

The docs says:

>You can require specific files or sub modules distributed with a module by including a path suffix after the module name. For instance require('example-module/path/to/file') would resolve path/to/file relative to where example-module is located.

This also breaks the module encapsulation as we can require everything, not just the functionality a module wanted to export.

Won't it be wise to deprecate these 2 features and finally drop them in io.js v2.0.0?

P.S.: I also haven't seen that those features were used in any popular project.

issue.title: Level 2 - smuggler mission
issue.body:
```
Maybe this is a combination of several not implemented game features but the 
mission is a complete mess:

The mission: Stop the smuggler on his way to San Sterling. (Level 2)

Your only information at this point is a smuggler ship which will appear in the 
next 24 hours.

Then SEVERAL trader ship have red boxes. You think that one of them may be the 
smuggler and start to investigate. By flying towars them you can communicate 
with them or you can just attack them or leave them be.

After a while the computer voice says "unknown objekt" and then a new ship 
appears with the "unknown" description. You can try to contakt the ship as well 
but they'll keep on pretending that they can not hear you. So you have to 
attack them. Before actually destroying the ship the battle ends automatically, 
the colonel appears on the screen and tells you "well done".


Open Imperium Galactica handels the mission this way:

- You get the mission to stop the smuggler.
- Within the next 24 hours an "unknown " ship appears
- You attack it and MANUALLY STOP the attack right before it gets 
destroyed
- The ship flees
- NOTHING

My guess: communication's missing, red boxes are missing (already know that), 
the video is not being triggered, actually having less traders in the own 
empire becomes a problem

```

issue.title: Change in escaping
issue.body:
::solr_escape which is now replacing the deprecated ::escape has one difference:
```
>   RSolr.escape("foo bar")
=> "foo\\ bar"
>   RSolr.solr_escape("foo bar")
=> "foo bar"
```
Is this significant? Or are we supposed to do to `field:foo AND field:bar` in our queries?
It's also not escaping floats as it used to:
```
>   RSolr.escape("1.11")
=> "1\\.11"
>   RSolr.solr_escape("1.11")
=> "1.11"
```
which affects projectblacklight/blacklight#1126

comment.body:
I haven't followed the code paths yet, but we should make sure it's easy for clients to produce parameters like `q=text_field:(foo bar)` or `q=text_field:"foo bar"`.

I suspect with this escaping change, we've probably made that more difficult, but it is probably a common pattern for applications accepting user input.

issue.title: #27 Basic journal search facility
issue.body:
Here goes.

The main entry point is the `org-journal-search` function, which asks for a search string and two dates (start end). Dates are read using the `org-read-date` function, which allows a rather free-form date entry (like `-7d` or `-1m`) plus a calendar-based date selection.

The results are just a read-only buffer with clickable (mouse/keyboard) links. I am thinking about implementing a nicer mode for the result buffer, but for now this should do.

I also played with a tag-based search, which collects tags from all the files and builds an index... Don't know if it's worth it.

Please, give it a try and let me know.

pull_request.title: BGM修正
pull_request.body:
前回のpull requestを送った際にイベント01の修正内容とBGMの実装について説明したので説明を省略します。

## BGM修正
* Sleep時もNightのBGMを再生するようにしました。
* DateTimeControllerのMorningかNoonかNightかSleepかを取得するIsTimeの条件式が間違っていました。
下記に詳細を示します。

if (NowTime.Hour >= StartTime && NowTime.Hour <= EndTime || NowTime.Hour >= EndTime && NowTime.Hour >= StartTime){
NowTimeZone = Name;
return true;
}

表1に時間帯表を示します。

**表1.時間帯表**

| TimeZone | StartTime | EndTime |
|:------:|:------:|:------:|
| Moning | 6 | 10 |
| Noon | 11 | 15 |
| Night | 16 | 21 |
| Sleep | 22 | 5 |

問題例としてMorningを条件式に適応します。
NowTime.Hour が23時だとします。
23 >= 6 → false
23 <= 10 →　false

23 >= 10 → true
23 >= 5 → true

下記の二つが両方trueとなり、23時は朝となってしまいます。

スタート関数実行時にNowTImeZoneがMorningになっていたのは上が主な原因となっています。
Update時にSleepになった原因はプログラムの流れが考えられます。取得する前にIsSleepが実行されたからだと考えています。


BGMManagerの条件式については
Sleepの条件式が最後に書かれていたのでSleepの処理に書き換えられたからです。

if...else if文については
Morinig、Noon、Night、Sleepは必ずどれかが一つになるため、または両方存在していたらどれを判定したらいいかわからなくなりおかしくなります。なのでif の羅列 より if...else if にするべきだと感じました。

issue.title: Allow keyword arguments in new
issue.body:
I found some discussion about this in https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/issues/10146#issuecomment-73742855, but no dedicated issue.

What I would expect this to look like:

```julia
type Foo
    a::Int32
    b::Int32
    c::Int32

    function Foo()
        return new(c = 123) # a and b undefinied
    end
end
```

issue.title: url with  ' &' when upgrade to rails 4.2.0
issue.body:
upload file with swfupload,  in Rails 4.1:

```ruby


Started POST "/attachments?sign=b4ed4e8d57459c9611579cea867ddd744715661310bd252edff56bca90aac4ba&type=message_photo&user_id=985493"  at 2015-02-27 13:46:49 +0000

Processing by AttachmentsController#create as */*

Parameters: {"Filename"=>"1024-1024.jpg", 
"Filedata"=>#<ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile:0x00000002933170 
@tempfile=#<Tempfile:/tmp/RackMultipart20150227-24987-upprgp>, @original_filename="5C 2.png", @content_type="application/octet-stream", @headers="Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"Filedata\"; filename=\"1024-1024.jpg\"\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n">, 
"Upload"=>"Submit Query", 
"sign"=>"b4ed4e8d57459c9611579cea867ddd744715661310bd252edff56bca90aac4ba", 
"amp"=>nil, 
"type"=>"message_photo",
 "user_id"=>"985493"}

```

' &' be escaped and converted ' "amp"=>nil ', it's  no problem.

but in Rails 4.2.0

```ruby
Started POST "/attachments?sign=b4ed4e8d57459c9611579cea867ddd744715661310bd252edff56bca90aac4ba&type=message_photo&user_id=985493"  at 2015-02-27 14:05:20 +0000

Processing by AttachmentsController#create as */*

Parameters: {"Filename"=>"1024-1024.jpg",
 "Filedata"=>#<ActionDispatch::Http::UploadedFile:0x007f89a894d0e8 
@tempfile=#<Tempfile:/tmp/RackMultipart20150227-25540-1bdmkd9.jpg>, @original_filename="1024-1024.jpg", @content_type="application/octet-stream", @headers="Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"Filedata\"; filename=\"1024-1024.jpg\"\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n">, 
"Upload"=>"Submit Query", 
"sign"=>"b4ed4e8d57459c9611579cea867ddd744715661310bd252edff56bca90aac4ba", 
"amp;type"=>"message_photo", 
"amp;user_id"=>"985493"}

```

'&' don't be escaped, i got  '  "amp;type"=>"message_photo" '  。 

of cource, i can use raw to resolve the problem:

```ruby
<%=raw attachments_path(sign: sign, user_id: controller.passport.id, type: "message_photo")%>"
```

but  i  think  the problem should not have happened,  '&'  should be escaped.

comment.body: @ZhangHanDong it looks like SWFUpload is sending the encoded ampersand from the HTML attribute to the server - it should be unescaping any HTML entities first. The difference you're seeing between 4.1 and 4.2 is due to a change in Rack 1.6 where the commit rack/rack@71c6911 broke the parsing of semicolons as query separators (reported in rack/rack#782). In either case, it's not a bug in Rails.

issue.title: Count different issues in error.
issue.body:
Travis's test suite should count the different types of errors and display a quick line display of each and their count in the document.

For example:
```
Passive voice: 5
Weak meaning: 10
Spelling: 25 (because this person doesn't know how to use a spellcheck...)
```

This way we could get a quick overview of a documents readiness status when a PR is made.

cc @kdzwinel since you built this thing and may know if it is possible.

comment.body:
I was working on my vim setup just now and realized that editor plugins are the long-term way to go to solving the woes of knowing what to do locally. I opened an issue on the [Proofreader tracker](https://github.com/kdzwinel/Proofreader/issues/11) so others interested on just that can see it.

I'm currently learning how to write a vim plugin to build this. Sublime Text would probably the most useful plugin though.

commits.message:
Some fixes/optimizations for the TreeFarmer

* Fix: Shears will stop shearing after being destroyed
* Optimization: Don't bother trying to do work if there is no axe or no
tree (harvestBlock() is allowed to return null...)
* Optimization: Changed hasAxe handling to the same as hasShears (if we
have an axe we'll keep it as long as we don't damage it)
* Optimization: In damageTool(), only roll the dice if there is a tool
to be damaged
* Fix: When asking a block for its drops, give it its own coordinates

```
I can send the save after Wednesday, because now i am not at home. 
Note about the kamikaze. If they start it from ther maximum fire distance at 
10% hp they will never reach any of my ship. The key for succes is that they 
come close (not very just moderate) start fireing and approx 25% hp do 
kamikaze. The fighter nearer i got less chance to destroy it. The priority 
witch ship should collide to would be the biggest and the nearest.

In original at hard level the only way to destroy Garthop capital ships while
```

issue.title: Can I safely embed `.env` in the Mina deploy script?
issue.body:
I'm currently doing this:

```
desc "Copies sensitive file data to the deploy script."
task :copy_dotenv do
  dotenv = File.read('.env')
  dotenv_production = File.read('.env.production')

  queue %[echo -n "#{dotenv}" | tr -d ' ' > "#{deploy_to}/#{shared_path}/.env"]
  queue %[echo -n "#{dotenv_production}" | tr -d ' ' > "#{deploy_to}/#{shared_path}/.env.production"]
end
```

Which embeds all my keys in the deploy script. Is this stupid or safe? I imagine it's fine since the deploy script is transmitted via SSH.

comment.body: I think a better solution would be to create a shared/.env file in your deploy_to path. Than you can add '.env' to shared_paths which will link your .env on each deploy. Same as config/database.yml or secrets.yml file

issue.title: Fix broken encapsulation of modules in io.js
issue.body:
Currently module loader looks for `node_modules` directory upwards recursively until the root of the file system is reached. This feature breaks module encapsulation as its dependencies can be pulled from global folder `/node_modules`.

The docs on `modules` say:
>For example, if the file at '/home/ry/projects/foo.js' called require('bar.js'), then io.js would look in the following locations, in this order:
/home/ry/projects/node_modules/bar.js
/home/ry/node_modules/bar.js
/home/node_modules/bar.js
/node_modules/bar.js
This allows programs to localize their dependencies, so that they do not clash.

The second feature is that we can require specific files from the module.

The docs says:

>You can require specific files or sub modules distributed with a module by including a path suffix after the module name. For instance require('example-module/path/to/file') would resolve path/to/file relative to where example-module is located.

This also breaks the module encapsulation as we can require everything, not just the functionality a module wanted to export.

Won't it be wise to deprecate these 2 features and finally drop them in io.js v2.0.0?

P.S.: I also haven't seen that those features were used in any popular project.

comment.body: FWIW, the io.js stability index just got a revamp in the past week and it was decided that the module system would remain locked. I think this is going to be a tough sell.

issue.title: Possible improvement to Status bar at the bottom of the screen
issue.body:
```
Situation: 

You're looking at the colony screen. You want to go back to the starmap/bridge. 
You have to click on the starmap/bridge button on the lower right side. Be 
carefull not to touch the other buttons.

You are on the starmap. You want to go back to the bridge. Ok, let's click on 
the bridge button...aaaa...it's in the middle of the left side.

Production etc. is simple AT THE MOMENT. But someday we will have them @ full 
screen (I hope :D :D) and then they have their individually located brige or 
starmap button, too.

DOS IG has a nice feature regarding the status back. A left click always sends 
you back to the bridge. It makes sense because in DOS IG your Bridge is really 
your starting point for everything. And the status bar is easily reached. It's 
big, it'S always at the same location and you just havce to get your mouse 
somewhere down to the bottom of the screen.

Now Open IG has the IG2 styled seleection menu on the upper right side and of 
course there are always your pretty "F" keys. Still a simple, consistent way of 
"going back" would be nice imo.


My proposal: 

1) Left click on status bar returns the player back to the bridge like DOS IG.

or (maybe even better)

2) Left click on status back sends you ONE STEP back. It means: 

Colony screen --> left click status bar --> starmap
starmap --> left click status bar --> bridge
etc.
```

issue.title: ImportError: No module named pkg_resources
issue.body:
After following the installation instructions for Linux at the crossbar.io web site I tried creating a hello application but got the error below. Seems I'm missing a Python module? I'm running on a CentOS 6 installation which has both Python 2.6 and 2.7 installed. Anyone seen this before?

[syncalt@Analytics ~]$ crossbar init --template hello:php --appdir www/presentation/hello
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/bin/crossbar", line 5, in <module>
    from pkg_resources import load_entry_point
ImportError: No module named pkg_resources
[syncalt@Analytics ~]$

comment.body:
Yes, you're missing a Python module. `pkg_resources` is part of `setuptools` - so it should be easiest to just install these again. 

Try 

```sh
curl https://bootstrap.pypa.io/ez_setup.py | python
```

(as per this [StackOverflow answer](http://stackoverflow.com/a/10538412/1077987))

issue.title: AutoFixture's AutoDataAttribute and xUnit's PropertyDataAttribute don't play nice together
issue.body:
As described in [this StackOverflow answer](http://stackoverflow.com/a/18930198/1860652), the two attributes can't be combined in the usual ways.

I have shared my solution [here](http://stackoverflow.com/a/28767887/1860652) - if you're interested in implementing this in AutoFixture.xUnit.net, I could get it into shape for a PR

comment.body:
Nikos, I'd be wary of supplying the same objects for different testcases. In an immutable world that's fine but there could be unintended consequences of reusing a mock, for example.

This actually extends to the `IFixture` instance itself - if you freeze an object in the fixture, the same instance will be resupplied to every test case, again exposing the user to unintended side-effects. This is why I suggested a separate DataAttribute that takes a factory function, so it can instantiate the fixture for each test case.

Mark, I did think that a `zip` is the most sensible way to do this. My only concern is that the user might accidentally restrict the number of test cases to one, by using a regular `AutoDataAttribute`. As we've seen, in the current implementation this throws an `InvalidOperationException`, thereby warning the user that something is wrong. With a `zip` there is no error, but only the first testcase is executed. Do you think that is acceptable? Perhaps the docs could warn the user?

issue.title: Fixed base64 encoding appending a newline
issue.body:
Method `encode64` appends a newline which ruins nginx config.
Method `strict_encode64` does the same without newlines.

```ruby
require 'base64'
gu='ga'
gp='gu'

Base64.encode64        "#{gu}:#{gp}" # "Z2E6Z3U=\n"
Base64.strict_encode64 "#{gu}:#{gp}" # "Z2E6Z3U="
```

issue.title: Setup task should not be trying to chown or chmod
issue.body:
The setup task should just attempt to create the require directory structure. It is perfectly possible for the deploy user to be able to create the directories but not be permitted to run `chmod`/`chown` on them. However, if the user can create the directory structure successfully what is the need for `chmod`/`chown` to be run in the first place?

The way these commands are structure is founded on far too many assumptions. Here are the relevant lines from `mina/deploy.rb`.

```
      #{echo_cmd %{chown -R `whoami` "#{deploy_to}"}} &&
      #{echo_cmd %{chmod g+rx,u+rwx "#{deploy_to}"}} &&
```

These commands assume that:
* The deploy folder and all its subfolders must be owned by the deploying user.
* The group, which is neither defined nor managed by the setup task, must have read and execute permissions.

These assumptions are deeply flawed and I would argue that folder permissions fall well outside the purview of a deployment tool's responsibility. They should already be configured by a system provisioning tool as part of the system architecture.

For my purposes I had to clear out all of the default setup actions in order to write a sane setup script.

issue.title: Experiment not doing back-prop if doing exploration
issue.body:
Part of the difficultly in games where there's one killer move amongst a large sea of dross is that we feedback the dross along with the killer move.  As a result, the parent node ends up with a low average score.

Consider only doing back-prop through a node when it's the node that would have been selected based solely on the exploitation score.  When the exploration bias has tipped the balance in favour of an otherwise non-preferred child, stop back-prop at that point.

Will obviously significantly reduce the number of rollouts reaching the top of the tree during back-prop, but perhaps that isn't an issue.  If it is, here's a potential mitigating strategy: Continue back-prop if the exploitation score of the selected child is within (say) 1 s.d. of the exploitation score of the preferred child.

May require some additional hackery to only impose the early back-prop cut-off once all children have been sampled at least (say) 3 times.

comment.body: Breakthrough scores 24-6 (20s moves) so perhaps some use in high branching-factor games after all.

issue.title: #27 Basic journal search facility
issue.body:
Here goes.

The main entry point is the `org-journal-search` function, which asks for a search string and two dates (start end). Dates are read using the `org-read-date` function, which allows a rather free-form date entry (like `-7d` or `-1m`) plus a calendar-based date selection.

The results are just a read-only buffer with clickable (mouse/keyboard) links. I am thinking about implementing a nicer mode for the result buffer, but for now this should do.

I also played with a tag-based search, which collects tags from all the files and builds an index... Don't know if it's worth it.

Please, give it a try and let me know.

issue.title: Capture interactions between microsegments from some measures

milestone.title: Develop basic modeling functionality (technical potential)
milestone.description: Enable reading of measure and microsegment databases and calculation of technical potentials for measures. This milestone might also include the calculation of other important metrics for each measure, such as the cost of conserved energy.

issue.body: Some measures, while they might apply to a set of microsegments, can also have interaction effects on other microsegments. As an example, a measure for LED bulbs is a lighting measure and should be coded as impacting the appropriate lighting microsegments. At the same time, replacing fluorescent or incandescent bulbs with solid-state LED bulbs will also reduce cooling load and increase heating load. These interactions need to be captured. They should probably be included in the model itself, and not be coded into the measure definition, as that would require that individuals creating measures accurately note the relevant interactions for that particular measure, and might create an opportunity for errors (e.g. if someone forgets to code for changes in both heating _and_ cooling from a lighting-specific measure).

issue.body:
```
I once again have to mention the ground units AI.

Right now they do not attack buildings in Open IG.

I was told that it's making it easier.

But:

1) That way you''ll never have to deal with damages buildings. That's sad. They 
have a damage system for a reason.

and more important:

2) it makes it MORE difficult

In DOS IG some units attacked my units. The rest attacked my buildings. That 
way I could deal with the ones attacking me first and then I could destroy the 
others one by one. Yes, it was expensive because of the buldings loss but I had 
far better chances of actually winning the fight.

As always I can do a video if you can't follow me :)
```

comment.body:
```
If no cheating is involved, the game is extremely biased towards the player. 
More planets, bigger tax and better tech in the end.

Autobattle might be wrong due an issue with rockets. The algorithm works as 
follows:

- sum up all the hp+shield of your units (defense)
- sum up all your Damage per second on all units and weapon types (offense)
- compute how much time would it take to reduce the defense values with the 
offense
- that party wins who is faster
- the theoretical damage dealt during this time is then applied to the winning 
fleet, removing units as neccessary, but starting from low-cost to high-cost 
units, i.e., your battleships could survive.

Now rockets are trouble in this since they have 500 DPS and no capacity which 
is outright wrong. I.e., if you have 8 rockets, that should only mean 4000 
damage dealt over 8 seconds. After that only zero.

Ground battle is turn based where first the tanks fight each other with the 
same algorithm above, then defensive structures get attacked by 2-5 units in a 
turn based fashion.

Balance seems to be problematic as well. I couldn't extract any information 
from DOS IG besides the the obvious Damage points in the spacewar statistics.

The true AI strength can be observed in the Player vs. AI where AI uses the 
same human technology and has no limits on expansion.
```

See #6340.

This takes a slightly more conservative approach than disabling it entirely: if there's been no input for 2 hours, stop telling Windows it can't go to sleep.  Intentionally, doesn't do it from the pause screen.

This obviously duplicates the existing Windows setting, but I think 2 hours is a reasonable default that might save a couple laptops from dying here and there, by mistake. Not sure if other platforms need to do anything.

  file.

* Added TODO about possibility of "PRINT_TRACBACK" being ported to
  Python3. Needs to get rid of "printf" usages for that.

* More compact code for "PRINT_EXCEPTION", now using a "PRINT_REPR" that
  handles "NULL" values.

Cleanup, avoid helper function for bumping reference counts.

* Creation of frames now take the reference themselves, avoiding the
  taking of it by every user.

* A potential leak was discovered, added a TODO.

* This is not complete yet, but the plan is to remove "INCREASE_REFCOUNT"
  and "INCREASE_REFCOUNT_X" as soon as possible.

Cleanup, move operation codes to dedicated module.

* Also preparations to make the in-place operations optimized as well. It
  won't work currently though, because the illegal object remains in use,
  but the helper code is more correct now.
Tests: Disabled another CPython test that uses the network.

Cleanup, get rid of "INCREASE_REFCOUNT_X" entirely.

* Done with at least that variant. It's relatively useless, as it
  doesn't even check for NULL.

* Removed its declarations completely.

Cleanup, use template for quick iteration loop break code.

* This was previously not well vertically aligned, hurting the
  readability of generated code.

* Looking at this, as in-place operations may do something similar
  too.
Cleanup, move the definition of the garbage collector macros to prelude.

Cleanup, make "assertObject" as macro.

* This will be friendlier to the compiler, in terms of deciding about
  not in-lining an empty function.

* And it gives us the correct line in the assertions, instead of one
  in "assertObject", which we can't interpret without a call stack.

Cleanup, including the generated helpers is no longer necessary.

* This can help caching of object files, because the helpers vary per
  compiled program, and adding code can add one.

Optimization: Remove useless complications for in-place variable assignment

* The temporary variable expressions are not useful at all, they might
  tell a really good SSA that a variable reference may or may not change,
  but that's not used yet, and if needed, can be had easier by simply
  attaching it to the in-place operation.

* This speeds up integer in-place assignment by about 5%, which is of
  course important, as this kind of operation is absolutely typical for
  loops to be used in.
Tests: Added construct test for integer in-place assignments.
Cleanup, remove useless cast in generated code.

comment.body:
```
The entire way the objectives-cutscenes-messages is scripted has some issues. 
Messages are mostly optional, therefore, objectives need to be assigned when 
the time has come. If the mission involves cutscenes, it should be played 
before the objectives, or about 3-13 seconds after the objectives. Messages 
have similar issues, if presented the same time as the objectives, the mixed 
sound is problematic. 

So the general presentation strategy will be as follows:

- Play cutscene (if any)
- Incoming message (if any), wait 3 seconds
- Objectives (announce, complete, fail)

```

issue.title: Object mismatch with pymongo FixedOffset
issue.body:
I've discovered that the round-trip serialization/deserialization of a simple FixedOffset object produces a corrupted object. The output of [this test script](https://gist.github.com/jaraco/d979a558bc0bf2194c23/079efd37a641159c0c14a1ab93f7efce30bf3eda) produces:

```
============================= test session starts =============================
platform win32 -- Python 3.4.2 -- py-1.4.26 -- pytest-2.6.4
collected 1 items

test_fo.py F

================================== FAILURES ===================================
________________________ test_FixedOffsetSerializable _________________________

    def test_FixedOffsetSerializable():
    	import jsonpickle
    	import bson.tz_util
    	fo = bson.tz_util.FixedOffset(-60*5, 'EST')
    	serialized = jsonpickle.dumps(fo)
    	pprint.pprint(json.loads(serialized))
    	restored = jsonpickle.loads(serialized)
    	print(restored._FixedOffset__offset)
>   	assert restored == fo
E    assert <bson.tz_util.FixedOffset object at 0x0000000005F494A8> == <bson.tz_util.FixedOffset object at 0x0000000005EEFA90>

test_fo.py:16: AssertionError
---------------------------- Captured stdout call -----------------------------
{'_FixedOffset__name': 'EST',
 '_FixedOffset__offset': {'py/id': 1},
 'py/initargs': {'py/tuple': [{'__reduce__': [{'py/type': 'datetime.timedelta'},
                                              {'py/tuple': [-1, 68400, 0]}],
                               'py/object': 'datetime.timedelta'},
                              'EST']},
 'py/object': 'bson.tz_util.FixedOffset'}
<bson.tz_util.FixedOffset object at 0x0000000005F494A8>
========================== 1 failed in 0.52 seconds ===========================
```

As you can see, the object produced isn't equal to the one serialized. Furthermore, it appears as if the `.__offset` property of the object has been set to itself instead of the timedelta object.

comment.body: I've figured out the issue and I'm writing a test now to capture the failure in jsonpickle.

issue.title: Level 1: First trader protection mission - missing warning
issue.body:
```
Mission: First time you have to protect a trader (Mission 2 or 3)

If you move to the fleet and escort it there is a cutscene after some time 
follwed by a pirate attack. That works.

What is missing:

If you are NOT escorting the ship the cutscene is triggered too after some 
time, again followed by a pirate attack

AND THEN

A MESSAGE CAN BE HEARD "Commander, our sensors detect one of our transport 
ships is under ttacked" (something like that...I translated from german). 

This message is missing. Maybe such a message exists in later missions, too.

I remember such a message ("Commander, we detected an unknown object") was also 
missing in the smuggler mission later on. Maybe you forgot those vocal messages.
```

```
The unfortunate thing is that noise is still common in these recordings. I'm 
automatically upscaling to 16 bit in the game so the volume adjustment doesn't 
introduce artifacts. If possible, I'd like to keep audio in the original 8 bit 
if the editing only affects silence or cuts. In case more is needed (e.g., 
fade-in, effects), we can go for 16 bit (we have already some files of such, 
e.g., the laser sounds).

familiar with the internals of the OGG library to do such changes. Playing raw 
WAV is much simpler.
```

X-Git-Url: http://www.ginac.de/ginac.git?p=ginac.git;a=commitdiff_plain;h=dda45abd8a2c408f8b3eb7959a10dfb2468ecc3a
G_eval: fix incorrect use of STL iterator.

According to [lib.bidirectional.iterators] it's not OK to decrement
an iterator pointing to the beginning of the sequence. Fortunately random
access iterators provided by (current versions of) gcc/libstdc++ don't have
this silly limitation, so the code which works with pointers works with
iterators without any changes at all. However,
 - there's no guarantee that the current behavior won't change in the future
 - some non-GNU compilers are not that smart (i.e. the program segfaults
   upon when decrementing beginning-of-the-sequence iterator).

issue.body:
1. The changes to the public API are extremely minor, it simply adds a new object, `KmlDataSource`, which is the same as other data sources but for KML. It only has 3 functions. (`fromUrl`, `load`, `loadUrl`).
2. Also adds KML and KMZ support to `viewerDragDropMixin` and the Cesium Viewer app `source` parameter.
3. I've been keeping #873 up to date with what's done and what's not for overall KML support, check that out if you want to see what we support/don't support yet.
4. Do not look at `SurfacePositionProperty` at yet, I still have a lot of work to do on this class (including renaming it).  I'll update this PR when it's ready.  No matter what, it will be private for 1.7 since we still need to figure out the exact details of height reference support.  This is more about laying ground work.

Also, just a reminder that you'll want to either set `InfoBoxViewModel.defaultSanitizer` to `undefined` or comment out line 161 of `InfoBoxViewModel` when you're playing with this in order to avoid balloon descriptions getting neutered. I plan on addressing this in an unrelated pull (hopefully before 1.7).  You'll also want to use the proxy if you play with public Network Links.

- [x] Replace Sandcastle example and sample KML data, also snap new gallery image.
- [x] Update CHANGES
- [x] Improve ref doc and explain the `Entity.kml` property that gets added.
