issue.title: Setup task should not be trying to chown or chmod
issue.body:
The setup task should just attempt to create the require directory structure. It is perfectly possible for the deploy user to be able to create the directories but not be permitted to run `chmod`/`chown` on them. However, if the user can create the directory structure successfully what is the need for `chmod`/`chown` to be run in the first place?

The way these commands are structure is founded on far too many assumptions. Here are the relevant lines from `mina/deploy.rb`.

```
      #{echo_cmd %{chown -R `whoami` "#{deploy_to}"}} &&
      #{echo_cmd %{chmod g+rx,u+rwx "#{deploy_to}"}} &&
```

These commands assume that:
* The deploy folder and all its subfolders must be owned by the deploying user.
* The group, which is neither defined nor managed by the setup task, must have read and execute permissions.

These assumptions are deeply flawed and I would argue that folder permissions fall well outside the purview of a deployment tool's responsibility. They should already be configured by a system provisioning tool as part of the system architecture.

For my purposes I had to clear out all of the default setup actions in order to write a sane setup script.

power::eval(): fix several memory leaks

Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2010 20:09:18 +0000 (+0300)
X-Git-Url: http://www.ginac.de?p=ginac.git;a=commitdiff_plain;h=5f896fa7f59bbce727e4bba23df9c4bbdbb55c29
power::eval(): fix several memory leaks

While working on fsolve bug I've noticed the following in valgrind log:

==17455== 136 (56 direct, 80 indirect) bytes in 1 blocks are definitely lost in loss record 16 of 19
==17455==    at 0x4C249C7: operator new(unsigned long) (vg_replace_malloc.c:220)
==17455==    by 0x516CA70: GiNaC::power::eval(int) const (power.cpp:540)
==17455==    by 0x4FC1E39: GiNaC::ex::construct_from_basic(GiNaC::basic const&) (ex.cpp:310)
==17455==    by 0x406FBF: main (ex.h:255)

Heap allocated objects definitely need the status_flags::dyncallocated flag.
---
#9394: Change printing of mul objects to move the leading '-' sign of a coefficient out of a parenthesis. This allows printing x - (2*I - 1)*y instead of x + (-2*I + 1)*y.

sage trac 9834: pretty print latex form of rational functions

Now -1/x prints as -\frac{1}{x}, not \frac{-1}{x}.
Sage trac 9878: Make zeta(1) return unsigned infinity.
Sage trac 9879: Allow disabling automatic simplifications of add and mul objects performed in the constructor.
Sage trac #9881: make the csgn function conform to the original GiNaC specification.
Remove function.pl. We use array arguments to functions, so we don't need to autogenerate call functions for up to 14 arguments.
Remove some autogenerated files from the repository.

Sage trac #9900: Be more careful with conjugate(f(x)) -> f(conjugate(x)).

Based on the patch by Richard Kreckel for GiNaC, which can be found in the URL:

http://www.ginac.de/ginac.git?p=ginac.git;a=commitdiff_plain;h=ff8b400eb500618644231ed9e6f199c3b0b25135;hp=1a5127603d93125b75ee51c94200faf0b586ef32

Be more careful with conjugate(f(x)) -> f(conjugate(x)).

That identity is correct for holomorphic functions, but we have to be
careful with some functions not being holomorphic everywhere. On branch
cuts, it is wrong. For a discussion, see:
<http://www.ginac.de/pipermail/ginac-list/2010-April/001601.html>.

This patch changes the default behavior of user-defined functions. From
now on, a user-defined conjugate_func must be registered, in order to
evaluate conjugate(f(x)) -> f(conjugate(x)). This patch also adds such
functions for most initially known functions.

Sage trac 9891: Be more careful about final top-level substitution.

X-Git-Url: http://www.ginac.de?p=ginac.git;a=commitdiff_plain;h=9506030d2059ef868d5da8dcbe714c9c5b50ff50
Be more careful about final top-level substitution.

Substituting x==log(x) in exp(x) erroneously returned log(x) because of a
final subst(x==log(x)) after having eval'ed exp(log(x)) -> x. This final
substitution is wrong in the general case. On the other hand, the intent
is to syntactically substitute functions of a given kind etc. This patch
suppresses the final top-level substitution unless the intermediate result
is a container.

Thanks to Burcin Erocal for reporting this bug (originally described by
Kees van Schaik on sage-support@googlegroops.com).
---

Sage trac 9947: Make sure add::eval() collects all numeric terms.

X-Git-Url: http://www.ginac.de?p=ginac.git;a=commitdiff_plain;h=e08cda1854bdb82f6706ec269233577690ae00e4

Apparently, add::eval() assumed that none of the elements of its epvector
has a numeric rest. However, nothing guarantees that -- in particular
evalchildren() doesn't (and actually cannot) do so. Since there are many
places where a new add is constructed directly from an epvector, enforcing
this doesn't make sense either. One example where it did fail was found by
Burcin Erocal: real_part(1+2*(sqrt(2)+1)*(sqrt(2)-1)) returned 1+2*1, not 3.

Thanks to Burcin Erocal for reporting this bug.
Use hold() instead of manually setting status_flags.
ncmul::eval(): don't write beyond the end of the vector.

mul: algebraic_subs_mul(), has(): don't write beyond the end of array

algebraic_match_mul_with_mul() iterates over operands of mul, that is

for (size_t i=0; i<e.nops(); ++i)

However, the size of arrays (`vectors' in STL speak) passed to this
function is seq.size(), which is nops() - 1 for any mul object. Thus
algebraic_match_mul_with_mul() accesses beyond the arrays limit. Usually
it's not a problem, since any reasonable implementation of std::vector<bool>
packs booleans into ints (or longs). However, some STL implementations
(in particular, the one shipped with msvc) are more picky, and access
beyond the vector<bool> limits results in a segfault. Therefore let's
play safe and allocate proper number of elements (that is, nops()) for
those arrays (subsed and currsubsed).

power::series(): handle someg (trivial) singularities of the exponent...

... so GiNaC can expand expressions like

cos(x)^(sin(x)/x) // (x -> 0)
(1 + x)^(1/x) // x -> 0

and so on.

[Reported by Camille Gillot.]

clifford: fix a few GCCisms (or, not).

Some compilers (in particular, msvc) choke on `or' and `not'. Use
standard ! and || instead.

symmetry::compare_same_type(): const-correctness fix

The method in question is const, therefore one should use const_iterator
to access indices. Some compilers (for instance, msvc) are very strict
about this, and won't accept (invalid) code using non-const iterator.
Wrote up the analysis of scenario 2

Sage trac #9900: Be more careful with conjugate(f(x)) -> f(conjugate(x)).

Based on the patch by Richard Kreckel for GiNaC, which can be found in the URL:

http://www.ginac.de/ginac.git?p=ginac.git;a=commitdiff_plain;h=ff8b400eb500618644231ed9e6f199c3b0b25135;hp=1a5127603d93125b75ee51c94200faf0b586ef32

Be more careful with conjugate(f(x)) -> f(conjugate(x)).

That identity is correct for holomorphic functions, but we have to be
careful with some functions not being holomorphic everywhere. On branch
cuts, it is wrong. For a discussion, see:
<http://www.ginac.de/pipermail/ginac-list/2010-April/001601.html>.

This patch changes the default behavior of user-defined functions. From
now on, a user-defined conjugate_func must be registered, in order to
evaluate conjugate(f(x)) -> f(conjugate(x)). This patch also adds such
functions for most initially known functions.

Sage trac 9891: Be more careful about final top-level substitution.

X-Git-Url: http://www.ginac.de?p=ginac.git;a=commitdiff_plain;h=9506030d2059ef868d5da8dcbe714c9c5b50ff50
Be more careful about final top-level substitution.

Substituting x==log(x) in exp(x) erroneously returned log(x) because of a
final subst(x==log(x)) after having eval'ed exp(log(x)) -> x. This final
substitution is wrong in the general case. On the other hand, the intent
is to syntactically substitute functions of a given kind etc. This patch
suppresses the final top-level substitution unless the intermediate result
is a container.

Thanks to Burcin Erocal for reporting this bug (originally described by
Kees van Schaik on sage-support@googlegroops.com).
---

Sage trac 9947: Make sure add::eval() collects all numeric terms.

X-Git-Url: http://www.ginac.de?p=ginac.git;a=commitdiff_plain;h=e08cda1854bdb82f6706ec269233577690ae00e4

Apparently, add::eval() assumed that none of the elements of its epvector
has a numeric rest. However, nothing guarantees that -- in particular
evalchildren() doesn't (and actually cannot) do so. Since there are many
places where a new add is constructed directly from an epvector, enforcing
this doesn't make sense either. One example where it did fail was found by
Burcin Erocal: real_part(1+2*(sqrt(2)+1)*(sqrt(2)-1)) returned 1+2*1, not 3.

Thanks to Burcin Erocal for reporting this bug.
Use hold() instead of manually setting status_flags.
ncmul::eval(): don't write beyond the end of the vector.

mul: algebraic_subs_mul(), has(): don't write beyond the end of array

algebraic_match_mul_with_mul() iterates over operands of mul, that is

for (size_t i=0; i<e.nops(); ++i)

However, the size of arrays (`vectors' in STL speak) passed to this
function is seq.size(), which is nops() - 1 for any mul object. Thus
algebraic_match_mul_with_mul() accesses beyond the arrays limit. Usually
it's not a problem, since any reasonable implementation of std::vector<bool>
packs booleans into ints (or longs). However, some STL implementations
(in particular, the one shipped with msvc) are more picky, and access
beyond the vector<bool> limits results in a segfault. Therefore let's
play safe and allocate proper number of elements (that is, nops()) for
those arrays (subsed and currsubsed).

power::series(): handle someg (trivial) singularities of the exponent...

... so GiNaC can expand expressions like

cos(x)^(sin(x)/x) // (x -> 0)
(1 + x)^(1/x) // x -> 0

and so on.

[Reported by Camille Gillot.]

clifford: fix a few GCCisms (or, not).

Some compilers (in particular, msvc) choke on `or' and `not'. Use
standard ! and || instead.

symmetry::compare_same_type(): const-correctness fix

The method in question is const, therefore one should use const_iterator
to access indices. Some compilers (for instance, msvc) are very strict
about this, and won't accept (invalid) code using non-const iterator.

issue.body: Is it possible to make the compiler run through a folder (with sub folders) of .less files, and compile out .css files in the respective folders?

issue.title: Compiling a folder of .less files
issue.body: Is it possible to make the compiler run through a folder (with sub folders) of .less files, and compile out .css files in the respective folders?

comment.body:
I don't think this is a good idea to implement directly in dotless. Consider, for instance, a less file that requires variables or mixins defined in another file in order to function, but it doesn't import the defining file itself -- instead, both files are imported by a single master file. Now, compiling all three files separately would result in an error for one of them.

The smart choice, in my opinion, would be to write a PowerShell or bash script (depending on your environment).

issue.title: Music quality - noise and overdriven
issue.body:
```
As a former piano player I always thought Open IGs captured music sounds worse 
than the original. 

So I captured it myself and compared it to OpenIGs.

Open IGs was way overdriven (most of the dynamic was gone) and I had to go down 
a few db to make it even comparable to mine. Then I heard the noise. I wondered 
where the noises origin was and I quickly found it after I looked at Open IGs 
bitrate :)

Track: Music3

The first bars of the track I captured, then OpenIGs, then mine again, then 
Open IGs again.

Please don't use Laptop speakers or something like that. And turn up the 
volume. Otherwise you won't notice anything.
```

issue.title: Offline installation isn't working
issue.body:
Hi,
I've followd the instructions up to this line:
```npm install --global --cache ./.npmbox.cache --optional --cache-min 99999 npmbox```
It does something (installs and the npmbox shows in my global node modules), but npmbox isn't working. From cmd I try: ```npmbox``` but it is undefined.
Any idea why?

comment.body:
Hi,
Thanks a lot. I've found the issue.
As you suggested, I've checked the global env var in win.
I've found the batch files were created inside the "npm" folder itself and not inside the "npm/node_modules/npmbox" (nor the bin folder) for some reason.
I've added the correct path, and now it seems to work.
My problem now is this:
I've packed karma and jasmine. I'm now using ```npmunbox``` and it starts the process, but it shouts ```Error: Invalid version 0.0.0.1```.
Any idea why this happens? Might this be connected to the fact the batch runs from the npm folder?

commits.message:
Some fixes/optimizations for the TreeFarmer

* Fix: Shears will stop shearing after being destroyed
* Optimization: Don't bother trying to do work if there is no axe or no
tree (harvestBlock() is allowed to return null...)
* Optimization: Changed hasAxe handling to the same as hasShears (if we
have an axe we'll keep it as long as we don't damage it)
* Optimization: In damageTool(), only roll the dice if there is a tool
to be damaged
* Fix: When asking a block for its drops, give it its own coordinates

Merge pull request #2033 from HenryLoenwind/shearFarmer

Some fixes/optimizations for the TreeFarmer

issue.title: Filter Usernames
issue.body: GitHub allows 2 byte string characters and RTL characters inside user names. That's undesirable for us. We need a layer to remove these characters, and only allow `a-z`, `A-Z`, `0-9`, and ` ` inside the user's `name`. NB, `username` should be left unmodified.

Wow, thats a set of failures. Most missions have a tolerance of 12-24 ingame 
hours. Mission announcements usually take 3-5 seconds real time to avoid sound 
clashes. Super fast 60 min, 10 ingame hours pass each real second. So by the 
time you see the objectives, the time limit could be all over. 

I'll reinspect mission timings post beta release, till then, I suggest you set 
a lower speed for levels 1 and 2.

For the AI autobuild settings, AI doesn't respect the missions in general. It 
demolishes heavily damaged buildings and builds up the colony according to the 
population needs. AI will build church and military spaceport eventually, but 
never a laboratory in levels 1 and 2. AI is a money hog in general, therefore, 
I suggest you don't use it in levels 1 thru 3.

issue.title: Retry mode for livestreamer
issue.body: Just wondering if it is by design that live streamer do not retry on 403 error or if the broadcaster source died for a while and come back on, because I notice that in both of this cases it seems to just give up but for other cases like if there is no stream yet, it will continue trying.

comment.body:
If you're on Windows you can make it loop infinitely by using "goto", for example:

    :start
    livestreamer {URL} best -o ~/“streams/{videoName}-$NOW.flv" -O --retry-streams 1 --retry-open 86400

issue.title: Moved the Grenadier to the Allies
issue.body:
Reasoning:

* Soviets already got a fast infantry scout (dog).
* Soviets already got a strong unit against buildings (flame thrower). #7503
* Allies lacked a suitable infantry unit to drop into an undefended base.
* They seem to fit better with the Allies theme as they work somehow similar to artillery (explosions, chain reaction) while the flame thrower fit better with V2 (splash damage, fire).
* The soviets already have a lot of (redundant) infantry actors.

comment.body: This will also be useful in the future as a garrison clearer (the later C&C's generally used grenadiers and flame throwers).  I suspect this will require more balancing than just changing the owner.

issue.title: Port issue for TLS on port 465
issue.body:
I think there might be an incorrect port setting in the `plugin/tls`, which is breaking when deploying on port 465. This port should start clear, and then provide STARTTLS to switch on SSL, same as port 25. However, the code for connecting reads:

```
if ( ! defined $local_port || $local_port != 465 ) {  # SMTPS
```

This should probably read:

```
if ( ! defined $local_port || $local_port != 587 ) {  # SMTPS
```

Using 465 here makes the server start in SSL directly, which is not the normal port 465 behaviour. Where a server on 587 should start directly in SSL. The use of negated conditions makes it harder to read the logic here, but basically 465 is not SMTPS, it's the legacy/secondary SMTP. 

I'll happy send a pull request if needed.

comment.body: I think you shouldn't necessarily assume what people know, but I take your point. In practice the external email system I was using to test (and ultimately proxy to) had 465 set to behave as an alternate 25, helpfully.

issue.title: Trader counts as enemy fleet or is missing during Mission 2 battles
issue.body:
```
Game version: 0.94.400 


Operating System: Windows XP + SP3


Java runtime version: 6.26

Installed using the Launcher? Yes


Game language (en, hu): en


What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Mission 2 request to protect traders message arrives.
2. Direct fleet to attack pirate fleet.
3. Battle with pirate fleet starts.


What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Once the battle with the pirate fleet starts, the trader ship should be able to 
be controlled as an allied unit.  Defeating the pirate units should result in a 
victory and monetary reward. 

Instead all of the options for the trader are greyed out (move, attack, 
retreat, etc.).  When pirates are defeated, the trader remains and the battle 
stalls until the trader ship is either destroyed or has taken enough damage so 
that it automatically retreats. 

When the next random Mission 2 battle starts, the trader ship has the same 
amount of damage it had after being attacked by game player's fleet.  Once 
pirate units are defeated, the only way to conclude fight is to destroy the 
trader.  This triggers the main character to get fired --> game over.  Also 
automatically escaping the battle causes a failed mission --> game over.

These issues were not observed in the previous build (0.94.370)


```

issue.body:
```
Game version: 0.94.400 


Operating System: Windows XP + SP3


Java runtime version: 6.26

Installed using the Launcher? Yes


Game language (en, hu): en


What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Mission 2 request to protect traders message arrives.
2. Direct fleet to attack pirate fleet.
3. Battle with pirate fleet starts.


What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Once the battle with the pirate fleet starts, the trader ship should be able to 
be controlled as an allied unit.  Defeating the pirate units should result in a 
victory and monetary reward. 

Instead all of the options for the trader are greyed out (move, attack, 
retreat, etc.).  When pirates are defeated, the trader remains and the battle 
stalls until the trader ship is either destroyed or has taken enough damage so 
that it automatically retreats. 

When the next random Mission 2 battle starts, the trader ship has the same 
amount of damage it had after being attacked by game player's fleet.  Once 
pirate units are defeated, the only way to conclude fight is to destroy the 
trader.  This triggers the main character to get fired --> game over.  Also 
automatically escaping the battle causes a failed mission --> game over.

These issues were not observed in the previous build (0.94.370)


```

issue.title: [New feature] Percent increase compared to the previous
issue.body:
Hi, 

can you add a section to compare the number of previous points with the new, calculating a percentage.

Example:
Previous: 1500 points
New: 2000 points
Growth rate: 133%

comment.body:
It basically compares a stored memerlist with the current one to make the statistics, the stored one is saved in the broser local storage every time the user clicks on the "Reset statistics" button.

Code in detail (by lines):

1-10: script greasemonkey metainfo
15-18: access to the ogame window
22-34: function to add css
38-68: copy member list (to avoid weird data-loss ogame does on mouseover)
72-76: script self metainfo
78-122: extend String prototype to do some basic operations
135-162: get some ogame metadata
164-201: build an object to easily work with the browser local storage to persist data
203-786: translations
788-837: output color profiles
839-852: basic score operations (compare points)
854-1423: formatter (pretify data)
1425-1762: conversor (builds statistics)
1775-2003: object to work with the DOM
2005-2095: add some css
2097-2557: Form builder (user interface)
2559-2663: Section builder (form container, user interface)
2665-2718: Interface builder (waits for some DOM objects to be available before calling the Section/Form builder)
2727-end: Script caller (waits for de DOM to be ready before start the script)

commits.message: Merge patches branch, atan2 fixes from Volker.

Fix unarchiving of symbolic functions defined at runtime without any custom methods.

Since the python_func member of function is a bitmask indicating which custom
methods are defined in Python, symbolic functions defined at runtime are
archived as regular GiNaC functions defined in C++. Unarchiving these later is
not possible, as GiNaC does not expect any other functions than those already
in the registry.

Adding a Python callback to create a new symbolic function with the given and
number of arguments if one is not found in the registry solves the unarchiving
problem while keeping the archive/pickle format the same.
Add vim swap files and ctags file to hgignore.
Use PyObject_Cmp to compare numerics wrapping Python objects.

beta() should not return numeric evaluation if both arguments are crational.

In beta_eval(), this test is used to decide if a numeric evaluation should be
returned:
    if (!ex_to<numeric>(x).is_rational() || !ex_to<numeric>(x).is_rational())

This patch fixes the typo that both tests are for the first argument x and
replaces the is_rational() test with is_crational().
Add method to ex for counting number of symbols in an expression.
The pynac C++ part of the infinities rewrite
Evaluate psi1 numerically if argument is not crational.
Added tag pynac-0.2.4 for changeset f50fb4810d97

Fix infinite loop in power::eval.

While trying to simplify exponents of Python longs, power::eval enters an
infinite loop since it doesn't expect arithmetic with crationals to produce
inexact results.

This is #13107 on Sage trac.

Do not include release version in library name. Now it is libpynac.so only.

Contributed by Julien Puydt.

Fix detection of Python.

Instructions provided by Julien Puydt.

Less verbose output during build. Use V=1 to get the verbose version.

Contributed by Julien Puydt.

Fix printing of parenthesis around exponents of power objects.

Reported and fixed by Sebastien Gouezel.

Whether parenthesis were printed or not for exponents of power objects
depended on the expression they were a part of. For example,

sage: latex(x^(2/3)+1)
x^{\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)} + 1
sage: latex(x^(2/3))
x^{\frac{2}{3}}

This patch stops passing the nesting level to the print method used to
output the exponent.
Add include statements to fix building with DO_GINAC_ASSERT defined.

fixes #12 : infinite loop when normalizing an add with content in GF(2)

If the content of an add expression is in GF(2^k), normalizing this add within
a mul::eval() leads to infinite loops. The normalization is done by
multiplying by -c where c is the content. When characteristic is 2 and c is 1,
-c is also 1. So no normalization occurs, causing the eval() function to run
into this case again.

This patch introduces a check if the characteristic is 2 when setting the
normalization factor -c. In this case, the factor -1 in ZZ is used instead to
fix the sign of the leading term that is triggering the normalization in the
first place.

This was #13609 on Sage trac.

issue.title: Error in raspberry pi
issue.body:
The error is triggered in https://github.com/franciscod/pyfprint-cffi/blob/master/pyfprint/pyfprint.py#L194 because r is equal to -22. 
You know who is that?

comment.body:
In fp_enroll_finger_img, a negative value means an error ocurred. Let's have a look at libfprint's code!

https://github.com/anarsoul/libfprint/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=fp_enroll_finger_img&type=Code

https://github.com/anarsoul/libfprint/blob/899c0a65a2edc7c799d6f2ed659ac0ccd36fce14/libfprint/sync.c#L176

You can see several ```c
return -EINVAL;
```

EINVAL is defined as 22 ([reference](http://www-numi.fnal.gov/offline_software/srt_public_context/WebDocs/Errors/unix_system_errors.html))

I think building libfprint with debugging enabled is a good first step for troubleshooting the error. 

Which fingerprint reader device do you have? The Pi has some power issues on USB, you could try using a powered USB hub instead. Also, you can test on another computer with a good 500mA USB port.

issue.title: Moved the Grenadier to the Allies
issue.body:
Reasoning:

* Soviets already got a fast infantry scout (dog).
* Soviets already got a strong unit against buildings (flame thrower). #7503
* Allies lacked a suitable infantry unit to drop into an undefended base.
* They seem to fit better with the Allies theme as they work somehow similar to artillery (explosions, chain reaction) while the flame thrower fit better with V2 (splash damage, fire).
* The soviets already have a lot of (redundant) infantry actors.

comment.body: The AI will also need to be made aware of this change. :+1:

issue.title: Unable to set subnet on a load_balancer.
issue.body:
I'm trying to learn how to use chef-provisioning with AWS and have run into a snag no amount of web searching has solved.  I took this code mostly from the examples here on this page but as we have several different VPC's I must be able to set which subnet Hosts and Load Balancers are in.  No matter what I do the Load Balancer ends up in our default subnet and I end up with an error saying the Host and LB are not in the same VPC.
```
  load_balancer "testlb-aws01" do
               load_balancer_options :availability_zones => ['us-east-1a'],
                          :listeners => [{
                               :port => 80,
                               :protocol => :http,
                               :instance_port => 8080,
                               :instance_protocol => :http,
                           }],
                           :subnet => ['subnet-z5555555']
    machines ['testvm-aws01']
  end
```
If this isn't a 'bug' and in fact is just my terrible understanding of the code is there any good resource for what options are allowed and how to set them.  The README is empty and the web has virtually nothing on chef-provisioning-aws.

comment.body:
@jkeiser, Thank you for the reply and the link to the documentation.  I tried as you suggested and added an 's' to subnet and removed the availability_zones line but ended up with;
```
    AWS::ELB::Errors::ValidationError
    ---------------------------------
    Either AvailabilityZones or SubnetIds must be specified
```

I noticed on the available documentation that it says, :availability_zones (required, Array) so I tried with both availability_zones AND subnets and I got a working Load Balancer but again in the default subnet instead of the one specified.

commits.message:
Improve code coverage for System.Diagnostics.Debug

Primary changes:
- The AttributeTests class wasn't public, and thus none of its tests were being run.  Fixed it to be public, and fixed one of its tests that was throwing ~4 billion exceptions and thus taking a very long time to run :)
- Added coverage for DebuggerTypeProxyAttribute, which was left out of the tests
- (Potentially controversial) The current testing is done against a test mock.  This means that while the Debug API is being exercised, the actual underlying implementation is not.  I added a call to exercise that underlying implementation as well, just to ensure it's not failing, but no verification is done on its output.
- Added stubbed out tests for Debugger, which is currently not implemented.  This will help ensure we go back and add tests when the real implementation is available.
- Added tests for a few other corner cases

This boosts the code coverage of the tests from ~40% to ~67%.  We are unlikely to get much higher than this: the remaining missed code paths are either related to resources or to popping up assert modal dialogs, which we don't want to do in tests.

issue.title: Fix broken encapsulation of modules in io.js
issue.body:
Currently module loader looks for `node_modules` directory upwards recursively until the root of the file system is reached. This feature breaks module encapsulation as its dependencies can be pulled from global folder `/node_modules`.

The docs on `modules` say:
>For example, if the file at '/home/ry/projects/foo.js' called require('bar.js'), then io.js would look in the following locations, in this order:
/home/ry/projects/node_modules/bar.js
/home/ry/node_modules/bar.js
/home/node_modules/bar.js
/node_modules/bar.js
This allows programs to localize their dependencies, so that they do not clash.

The second feature is that we can require specific files from the module.

The docs says:

>You can require specific files or sub modules distributed with a module by including a path suffix after the module name. For instance require('example-module/path/to/file') would resolve path/to/file relative to where example-module is located.

This also breaks the module encapsulation as we can require everything, not just the functionality a module wanted to export.

Won't it be wise to deprecate these 2 features and finally drop them in io.js v2.0.0?

P.S.: I also haven't seen that those features were used in any popular project.

comment.body:
This is not the most used features of the module system, but I've seen both of them used a lot. So changing this will break a lot of code.

Yes, the ability to have private modules for packages is a feature which would be nice. It is being discussed for core (https://github.com/iojs/io.js/pull/848). But I don't see any clean way that can be implemented without breaking backwards compatibility.

issue.title: Make logs more accessible
issue.body:
Currently most of the logs are hidden in the .meteor/local/log folder. We should make them more visible. To start with we should transfer them to a central place (velocity:core) into a MongoDB collection.

### Outputting logs

For outputting the logs I suggest a similar plugin system to the test result reporters.
Initially we would have these options:

* velocity:log-console-reporter (Output to console)
* velocity:html-reporter (Make probably sense to include it as part of the existing html-reporter)
* velocity:log-file-reporter (Output to file)

If someone has an alternative suggestion for the naming, let me know.

### Transferring logs

#### API

We should have a Meteor method in velocity:core for sending log lines from a testing framework to velocity:core.

A suggestion (still WiP):
```javascript
Meteor.call('velocity/logs/submit', {
  framework: 'my-framework',
  lines: [
    'Line 1',
    'Line 2'
  ]
})
```

* Assign log lines to a specific framework
* Allow to send multiple lines with one Meteor call (does this make a performance difference vs. one call per line?)

#### Mirror logs

Transfer stdout and stderr of mirrors to the main app.

1. Run synergy on both machines (I'll call server and client)

3. Move mouse to client, try to click another application other than the one currently focused.(Example: I am using Chrome and I have outlook running but it's behind chrome, try running outlook)

Expected: Other application is brought to the front and gains focus
Actual: about 50% of the time, the previous application which had focus stays on top while the other app becomes focused by the input.  In other words, I cannot force the window to be brought to the front.

Current work around: Clicking the application which has focus then clicking back in to the other app usually fixes the issue; however, this becomes extremely annoying after time....  *(Note, the current work around does not work with all apps - IE and Chrome are not playing nicely and chrome refuses to allow IE to take focus)

commits.message:
docs: expand documentation around plugins

When I read the plugins documentation, it wasn't entirely clear to me
what "plugin based system" means. Furthermore, it wasn't obvious that
Heka ships with many plugins. I've updated the docs to reflect this.

docs: move plugin language requirement to separate paragraph

The paragraphs describing the Heka plugin types were quite long
and container a lot of info. This patch adds a separate paragraph
describing the language requirements for each plugin type.

docs: use definition list for plugin types

IMO a definition list is more appropriate than a bullet list for
defining the plugin types. Switch it.

docs: split input plugin docs into own pages

The current method of including the content of the input plugins on one
page is a bit unwieldy. It can be a little difficult to follow all the
available input plugins.

This patch splits the input plugins into their own page. We use
a toctree to display links to each input plugin. This preserves the
existing sidebar linking.

A label for each input plugin has been added to its .rst, which is
arguably where it should have always been. The "no ref" index page was
hacked up to skip the first line of these files. This prevents
duplicate label warnings from Sphinx.

docs: fix whitespace in docker log input docs

Tabs were being used in the example configuration docs. They were
resulting in weird formatting. They have been normalized to spaces.

docs: better page titles for input plugins

The page titles for input plugins were *Input. These were showing up in
tocs and sidebars and weren't the most friendly of strings for humans to
read.

This commit converts the titles to something more human friendly and
adds a plugin name entry defining the name for the plugin to be used
in configs. This latter bit was necessary because the page titles were
formerly serving this role.

Having a dedicated RST entity to declare the plugin name is probably
appropriate. But the patch author was too lazy to perform this work.
skip blank lines in multi line input

Handle errors in single lines of multiline Statsd better

Since many java/scala apps emit bulk statsd lines this handles both errors in individual lines by skipping that line, NOT the entire multiline message, and emits a log warning (not an error) and processes any other statsd lines that are ok.  Also skip lines that are blank in a multi request.

Add disk-based buffering for ElasticSearch output

As discussed on the Heka mailinglist, this is a commit to introduce a
use_buffering mode to the ElasticSearch output plugin. It changes the
default behavior to buffer to disk, like the TCP Output plugin, with all
the other options of the TCP Output plugin and the additional option to
set use_buffering to false to disable it (this just dumps any failed
packets to nowhere, though - no retry logic).

This also buffers in "chunks" rather than individual messages, so there
still is the tiny possibility that if a message has been received and
hasn't filled the commit buffer yet, it can be lost if Heka dies, but the
default commit buffer is sent every 1 second so this state is a lot better
than quietly dropping messages if they fail to send even once.
check that "warn" is also nil in test

Incorporate code review comments, add docs

Changes the ElasticSearch plugin further to only use a channel to send
messages to ES if not in buffered mode. Also adds changelog and docs.

issue.title: Means with missing data
issue.body: I loaded a data file and it can give me distributions and correlations, but when I click on Descriptives and ask it for means, it give me nothing but white space. In the same file it will give me means when I use a variable with no missing data. Given this difference, I assume it is due to the missing data in the other variables that JASP will not provide means.

comment.body:
I think the problem stemmed from there being less than 24 unique values. I had a 7-pt likert scale so there were only 7 unique values.

----- Original Message -----
From: "Jonathon Love" <notifications@github.com>
To: "jasp-stats/jasp-desktop" <jasp-desktop@noreply.github.com>
Cc: "CJCarpenter" <cj-carpenter2@wiu.edu>
Sent: Sunday, March 1, 2015 10:11:50 AM
Subject: Re: [jasp-desktop] Means with missing data (#400)

> I'm not sure why it uploaded it as a nominal variable

the criteria for something being considered continuous is:
 - all cells must contain a numeric value
 - there must be at least 24 unique values

i'm not sure where your dataset has come from, but if it was created using the `write.csv()` command in R, then this would cause issues. `write.csv()` has a bug... err, i mean feature... where missing values are replaced with `NA`. `NA` is a string, and so the column gets treated as nominal.

of course, this is fixed by changing the column to continuous; all non-numeric values are converted to missing values (including the NAs), and so you end up with an equivalent dataset to what was in R.

---
Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub:
https://github.com/jasp-stats/jasp-desktop/issues/400#issuecomment-76604903

commits.message:
Kbuild, lto: Add Link Time Optimization support v3

With LTO gcc will do whole program optimizations for
the whole kernel and each module. This increases compile time,
but can generate faster and smaller code and allows
the compiler to do global checking. For example the compiler
can complain now about type mismatches for symbols between
different files.

LTO allows gcc to inline functions between different files and
do various other optimization across the whole binary.

It might also trigger bugs due to more aggressive optimizations.
It allows gcc to drop unused code. It also allows it to check
types over the whole program.

The compile time is definitely slower. For gcc 4.8 on a
typical monolithic config it is about 58% slower. 4.9
drastically improved performance, with slowdown being
38% or so. Also incremenential rebuilds are somewhat
slower, as the whole kernel always needs to be reoptimized.
Very modular kernels have less build time slow down, as
the LTO will run for each module individually.

This adds the basic Kbuild plumbing for LTO:

- In Kbuild add a new scripts/Makefile.lto that checks
the tool chain (note the checks may not be fully bulletproof)
and when the tests pass sets the LTO options
Currently LTO is very finicky about the tool chain.
- Add a new LDFINAL variable that controls the final link
for vmlinux or module. In this case we call gcc-ld instead
of ld, to run the LTO step.
- For slim LTO builds (object files containing no backup
executable) force AR to gcc-ar
- Theoretically LTO should pass through compiler options from
the compiler to the link step, but this doesn't work for all options.
So the Makefile sets most of these options manually.
- Kconfigs:
Since LTO with allyesconfig needs more than 4G of memory (~8G)
and has the potential to makes people's system swap to death.
I used a nested config that ensures that a simple
allyesconfig disables LTO. It has to be explicitely
enabled.
- Some depencies on other Kconfigs:
MODVERSIONS, GCOV, FUNCTION_TRACER, KALLSYMS_ALL, single chain WCHAN are
incompatible with LTO currently, mostly because they
they require setting special compiler options
for specific files, which LTO currently doesn't support.
MODVERSIONS should in principle work with gcc 4.9, but still disabled.
FUNCTION_TRACER/GCOV can be fixed with a unmerged gcc patch.
- Also disable strict copy user checks because they trigger
errors with LTO.
- modpost symbol checking is downgraded to a warning,
as in some cases modpost runs before the final link
and it cannot resolve LTO symbols at this point.

For more information see Documentation/lto-build

Thanks to HJ Lu, Joe Mario, Honza Hubicka, Richard Guenther,
Don Zickus, Changlong Xie who helped with this project
(and probably some more who I forgot, sorry)

v2:
Merge documentation file into this patch
Improve documentation and Kconfig, fix a lot of obsolete comments.
Exclude READABLE_ASM
Some random fixes
v3:
Remove CONFIG_LTO_SLIM, is on by default.
Signed-off-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Michal Marek <mmarek@suse.cz>

Signed-off-by: DerRomtester <dieb.stefan.96@gmail.com>

kbuild: link of vmlinux moved to a script

Move the final link of vmlinux to a script to improve
readability and maintainability of the code.

The Makefile fragments used to link vmlinux has over the
years seen far too many changes and the logic had become
hard to follow.

As the process by nature is serialized there was
nothing gained including this in the Makefile.

"um" has special link requirments - and the
only way to handle this was to hard-code the linking
of "um" in the script.
This was better than trying to modularize it only for the
benefit of "um" anyway.

The shell script has been improved after input from:
Arnaud Lacombe <lacombar@gmail.com>
Nick Bowler <nbowler@elliptictech.com>

Signed-off-by: Sam Ravnborg <sam@ravnborg.org>

Kbuild, lto, workaround: Don't warn for initcall_reference in modpost

This reference is discarded, but can cause warnings when it refers to
exit. Ignore for now.

This is a workaround and can be removed once we get rid of
-fno-toplevel-reorder

Signed-off-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/1391846481-31491-7-git-send-email-ak@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@linux.intel.com>

Kbuild, lto: Drop .number postfixes in modpost

LTO turns all global symbols effectively into statics. This
has the side effect that they all have a .NUMBER postfix to make
them unique. In modpost drop this postfix because it confuses
it.

Signed-off-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/1391846481-31491-8-git-send-email-ak@linux.intel.com

To check the linker version. Used by the LTO makefile.

Signed-off-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/1391846481-31491-9-git-send-email-ak@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@linux.intel.com>

Kbuild, lto: Add a gcc-ld script to let run gcc as ld

For LTO we need to run the link step with gcc, not ld.
Since there are a lot of linker options passed to it, add a gcc-ld wrapper
that wraps them as -Wl,

Signed-off-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/1391846481-31491-10-git-send-email-ak@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@linux.intel.com>

Kbuild, lto: Disable LTO for asm-offsets.c

The asm-offset.c technique to fish data out of the assembler file
does not work with LTO. Just disable for the asm-offset.c build.

Signed-off-by: Andi Kleen <ak@linux.intel.com>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/1391846481-31491-11-git-send-email-ak@linux.intel.com
Signed-off-by: H. Peter Anvin <hpa@linux.intel.com>

Kbuild, lto: Set TMPDIR for LTO v4

LTO gcc puts a lot of data into $TMPDIR, essentially another copy
of the object directory to pass the repartitioned object files
to the code generation processes.

TMPDIR defaults to /tmp With /tmp as tmpfs it's easy to drive systems to
out of memory, because they will compete with the already high anonymous
memory consumption of the wpa LTO pass.

When LTO is set always set TMPDIR to the object directory. This could
be slightly slower, but is far safer and eliminates another parameter
the LTO user would need to set manually.

I made it conditional on LTO for now.

v3: Use standard kernel variable style
v4: Print message for redirection (M.Marek)

issue.title: Developing micro segments in conjunction with ongoing Excel work

milestone.title: Populate JSON microsegment database (residential)
milestone.description: The microsegment data from EIA should be restructured into a convenient, human-readable form. Converting these data into a JSON-formatted microsegment database will facilitate their later use. Because the underlying residential and commercial data are formatted quite differently, two separate efforts are required, thus the residential and commercial database population milestones are now separate as well.

issue.body:
We need to develop a market micro segments database for our analysis framework to reference, which can be updated as new AEO, RECs/CBECs, and other relevant data sources are refreshed.  These micro segments could be defined through a tree structure, such as for a highly insulating window: Climate Zone X -> Commercial Buildings -> Commercial Building Type X -> Heating Energy -> Heating Energy Lost through Windows (note in that particular case, we might create a parallel segment for Cooling Energy to identify effects of higher window insulation on cooling energy).     

Some of this work is already being done in the existing Excel framework to bring the tool up to AEO 2014 and ensure the micro segments are correctly defined.  There is a question of whether the above efforts may be combined with this ongoing Excel work to save time.  One possibility discussed is to establish a code that updates all the micro segments (or perhaps just the micro segments not already updated) and pastes the resultant data into the existing Excel micro segments tab as a .csv.

issue.title: Google Play Android Developer API return 401
issue.body:
```
Version of google-api-java-client (e.g. 1.5.0-beta)?
Google Play Android Developer API v1-rev2-1.7.1-beta

Java environment (e.g. Java 6, Android 2.3, App Engine)?
Java 6

Describe the problem.
Server return 401 Unauthorized: This developer account does not own the 
application.

How would you expect it to be fixed?

                        HttpTransport HTTP_TRANSPORT = new NetHttpTransport();
                        JsonFactory JSON_FACTORY = new JacksonFactory();

                         GoogleCredential credential = new GoogleCredential.Builder().setTransport(HTTP_TRANSPORT)
			        .setJsonFactory(JSON_FACTORY)
			        .setServiceAccountId(GOOGLE_CLIENT_MAIL)
			        .setServiceAccountScopes("https://www.googleapis.com/auth/androidpublisher")
			        .setServiceAccountPrivateKeyFromP12File(new File(GOOGLE_KEY_FILE_PATH))
			        .build();
			
			Androidpublisher publisher = new Androidpublisher.Builder(HTTP_TRANSPORT, JSON_FACTORY, credential).
					setApplicationName(GOOGLE_PRODUCT_NAME).
					build();
			
			Androidpublisher.Purchases purchases = publisher.purchases();
			Get get = purchases.get("XXXXX", subscriptionId, token);
			SubscriptionPurchase subscripcion = get.execute(); //LINE 1

In Google APIS Console the Service "Google Play Android Developer API" is 
enabled.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_MAIL is the email address from API Access from the Google Console.
GOOGLE_KEY_FILE_PATH is the p12 file downloaded from the API Access.
GOOGLE_PRODUCT_NAME is the product name from the branding information.

The code return in LINE 1:

    "domain" : "androidpublisher",
    "message" : "This developer account does not own the application.",
    "reason" : "developerDoesNotOwnApplication"

```

issue.body:
Hey, great plugin - well done! First and foremost, testing on latest 0.3x.

**Bugs**

1. Class selection fails unless it's death by a car or something client-side.

2. Fall damage is just not as accurate as before?

3. Is the death world thing necessary? It seems to inflict bugs than anything else.

**Suggestion**

1. Allow users to easily disable portions of the code with using #define instead of using functions (Toggle{function}(bool: value)

    Should stop compiling unnecessary code that is already disabled by the server. Example:

    ```
#define TOGGLE_DAMAGE_FEED (true)

#if TOGGLE_DAMAGE_FEED == true
 ... operations ...
#endif
```

2. Make an addition to this by introducing maybe another optional feature which enables users to access weapon data (GetWeaponDamageFromDistance, GetWeaponDamage, GetWeapon blah blah.)

comment.body:
Yes, I took a quick look at traitlets, but I'm not convinced that they will be appropriate for what we need here.  What is the "atom" class?
Several years ago we experimented with using Enthought Traits, but decided against adopting this approach.  It seemed to add too much extra complexity--one almost had to learn, and work in, another language.  Traitlets are less daunting, but they still involve quite a bit of machinery.  They also impose fairly severe restrictions on the types of attributes they can handle, if I understand correctly--unless one adds support for additional types.

issue.title: R interface to EPA's air quality system
issue.body:
This has been on my list of things to do for a while now....

The EPA puts a ton of data out on the web from its [air quality system](http://www.epa.gov/ttn/airs/airsaqs/detaildata/downloadaqsdata.htm). But it takes some time to learn how the data are formatted and how the are measured. Also, downloading from the web site, unzipping, and then reading into R, can be a bit of a pain for the uninitiated. I thought it might be nice to have an R package that serves as an interface to the EPA's site and grabs data that would be useful for air pollution studies. The package could also implement some statistical methods that are commonly used in the preprocessing of the data (for health studies, for example).

Some npm packages strictly require a specific npm version because npm

However, Nix don't use npm for dependency resolution (this is always
achieved with npm 1.0 criteria by npm2nix), so these requirements turns

issue.title: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED with 2.5.2, works with 2.5.1
issue.body:
I'm having a somewhat odd issue. A get() request seems to work fine with requests-2.5.1, but after upgrading to requests 2.5.2, the same URL leads to `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED`. cc @mpharrigan

```
$ pip install requests==2.5.1
[ ... snip, installs just fine ...]

$ python -c 'import requests; print(requests.get("http://conda.binstar.org/omnia/linux-64/fftw3f-3.3.3-1.tar.bz2"))'
<Response [200]>

$ pip install requests==2.5.2
[ ... snip, installs just fine ...]

$ python -c 'import requests; print(requests.get("http://conda.binstar.org/omnia/linux-64/fftw3f-3.3.3-1.tar.bz2"))'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/site-packages/requests/packages/urllib3/connectionpool.py", line 544, in urlopen
    body=body, headers=headers)
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/site-packages/requests/packages/urllib3/connectionpool.py", line 341, in _make_request
    self._validate_conn(conn)
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/site-packages/requests/packages/urllib3/connectionpool.py", line 762, in _validate_conn
    conn.connect()
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/site-packages/requests/packages/urllib3/connection.py", line 238, in connect
    ssl_version=resolved_ssl_version)
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/site-packages/requests/packages/urllib3/util/ssl_.py", line 256, in ssl_wrap_socket
    return context.wrap_socket(sock, server_hostname=server_hostname)
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/ssl.py", line 364, in wrap_socket
    _context=self)
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/ssl.py", line 578, in __init__
    self.do_handshake()
  File "/Users/rmcgibbo/miniconda/envs/3.4.2/lib/python3.4/ssl.py", line 805, in do_handshake
    self._sslobj.do_handshake()
ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:600)

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
[... snip ...]
```

comment.body:
Do we believe that will *ever* happen? What's the impetus for operators to do that? The cross-signed roots are valid for ages (for example, Verisign's new cert is valid until 2036) and they work fine in browsers. The rationale for using the cross-signed root (that browsers might have old cert bundles) doesn't go away for any new root that will be issued.

So what am I missing that makes you believe that this change will occur?

issue.title: Trim behavior video
issue.body:
@forea 

The function `trim_behavior_video(plusmaze_source, behavior_source, trim)` will generate a new behavior video that matches the concatenated Miniscope video (i.e. produced by `concatenateHDF5` and `concatenate_bigtiff`) frame-by-frame. The `trim` parameter needs to match those used in the Miniscope concatenation, of course. (We've been using `trim = [15 5]` so far.)

Note! The output "trimmed" behavior video will have the number of frames according the plus maze output. If the behavior video has dropped frames, then the behavior video will be "uniformly stretched" to match the plus maze frame counts. (We should be able to improve on the localization of dropped behavior frames in the future.)

Performance-wise, it took about 30 min for my laptop to process c9m7d07 behavior video. It may be possible to improve the performance by batching the writes to the output file, which right now occurs frame-by-frame.

issue.body:
```

If you call getMediaHttpUploader().setDirectUploadEnabled(true) on a

fails, it never retries it. For retryable error codes, it should try again

if the resumable request fails in the space of that first block, the client 
will have to restart from the beginning anyway.

issue.title: Add drop-down menu for bibliographyLocale
issue.body:
Groundwork for adding a drop-down menu to the Styles tab of the Cite tab of the Zotero preferences, for selecting the bibliography locale. See also https://forums.zotero.org/discussion/45805/

Still needs some work, but I'd like some guidance on how to implement things:

 * I placed https://github.com/citation-style-language/locales/blob/master/locales.json at https://github.com/zotero/zotero/tree/4.0/resource/schema. Is that okay? How are similar files at this location being kept up to date (like "renamed-styles.json")?
 * Fresh installs of Zotero have an empty string for "extensions.zotero.export.bibliographyLocale". With the current code, an empty string value for bibliographyLocale is replaced by the value of Zotero.locale when the preference tab is loaded, or, if Zotero.locale isn't set, by "en-US". Is this behavior problematic if the pref can be set via the UI?
 * The drop-down menu options are limited to the locales for which we have CSL locale files. Should there be a way to specify a custom locale code for "extensions.zotero.export.bibliographyLocale" via the UI? If so, what should that look like? A "Custom..." entry at the bottom of the drop-down list, that, if selected, pops up a dialog box with a text box?
 * Should there be a top-five list of most-recently used locales at the top of the drop-down list?
 * For some reason the drop-down box stretches across the entire window. Not sure why. XUL beats me.
 * I removed `width` on `<label id="export-citePaperJournalArticleURL" width="45em">`, since it didn't do anything on OS X. Is this still necessary? Maybe we can check on other platforms.

comment.body:
definitely agree.

On Sun, Mar 1, 2015 at 11:03 AM, Rintze M. Zelle <notifications@github.com>
wrote:

> Do people agree that it might be preferable to not save the
> "export.lastStyle" pref when selecting a style with a default-locale (for
> those cases where the locale menulist responds to the selected style:
> Export Bibliography, Doc Prefs, RTF Scan)? That would give the user a bit
> more flexibility.
>
> E.g. if "export.lastStyle" is "fr-FR", and the user exports a bib in
> Nature format (default-locale="en-GB"), the output will be in "en-GB". If
> the user then exports a bib again with APA, it will default to "fr-FR". I
> think that's more desirable than switching "export.lastStyle" to "en-GB" in
> this case.
>
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> <https://github.com/zotero/zotero/pull/623#issuecomment-76613452>.
>



-- 
Sebastian Karcher, PhD
Department of Political Science
Northwestern University

[code]	        		
modelBatch.render(terrain.getTerrainChunk(x, y).getModelInstance(),env);
terrain.getTerrainChunk(x, y).getModelInstance().model.meshes.get(0).render(Lighting.getShader(), GL20.GL_TRIANGLES);

Actual output =
[img]
http://static.dyp.im/0bp089Ycx1/36c64a7a11e5622609098b97318970c8.png

issue.title: Non-chunked resumable uploads
issue.body:
```
External references, such as a standards document, or specification?
https://devsite.googleplex.com/storage/docs/json_api/v1/how-tos/upload#resumable

Java environments (e.g. Java 6, Android 2.3, App Engine, or All)?
Java 6, non-App Engine

Please describe the feature requested.
Requests using the resumable upload feature be sent as one streaming HTTP 
request (i.e., not having to be entirely resident in application memory) rather 
than chunks, as chunking incurs a significant performance penalty (4 to 5x 
longer) over just sending bytes until a connection error or early error result 
is returned.

Specifically, that a buffered stream wrap (if necessary) the underlying 
InputStream such that is has enough buffer to go back as far as required if the 
upload fails. This should be calculable based on some minimum internal commit 
chunk size plus (speed of the connection * maximum time before you know 
something went wrong with the connection, e.g., tcp timeout). Then, you are 
guaranteed in case of TCP termination or early HTTP error result that you can 
perform the resume an interrupted upload steps (query for how many bytes remain 
to be sent) and then send a subsequent single streaming HTTP session with the 
remaining bytes and the appropriate Content-Range header. Because there's no 
regular HTTP result code as for a chunk, you have to use that same calculus to 
determine when to invalidate earlier parts of the stream (record current 
location + Reset + Skip + Mark + Skip to current location) to avoid bloating 
application memory.
```

Original issue reported on code.google.com by `nherr...@google.com` on 9 Aug 2012 at 9:24

pull_request.title: Adds support for Continous Integration
pull_request.body:
I've been wanting to pull this one out for a while, and finally I did it.
This PR adds continuous integration for the Elixir Website,
It runs two different kinds of validation,

**html5validator**
[The W3C Validator](http://validator.w3.org/) developed by W3C and Mozilla.
It uses a precompiled package for python ([html5validator](https://github.com/svenkreiss/html5validator)).
This is the de-facto validator for html5, it will only check the markup validity

**html-proof**
[html-proof](https://github.com/gjtorikian/html-proofer) is a Ruby Gem. It will do all kind of validations, in addition to validate markup, it will check for favicons, external scripts being loaded, broken links and also internal broken links, images (internal and external). Anything that can break overtime (specially because we rely on external sources, ie, images, fonts, libraries), this will check for that, every time we make a commit.

The reality is that our website was not passing neither of both validations due to bugs [[1](https://github.com/svenkreiss/html5validator/issues/4),[2](https://github.com/gjtorikian/html-proofer/issues/190),[3](https://github.com/gjtorikian/html-proofer/issues/191)]  in these validators, and due nature of the website having hacky code to fix issues with old browsers. So that's why i created a script that will filter the errors in STDERR, and let us run the validators in Travis.

I wish we could [validate the css code](http://jigsaw.w3.org/css-validator/), but right now it's not possible, because the css it too hacky to support IE6 i think.

Links to the elixir documentation within the website have been disabled, because the /docs/ folder it not hosted within this project, We could configure html-proof to rewrite those relative links to absolute, but right now [a bug](https://github.com/gjtorikian/html-proofer/issues/192) prevented me from doing so. Anyway, I ran it locally, and I know it's all good.

You can see the travis build here: Usually it's been taking 1m 45sec, 
https://travis-ci.org/eksperimental/elixir-lang.github.com

issue.title: FieldInfo generates AccessControlException when running under SecurityManager
issue.body:
```
Version of google-api-java-client (e.g. 1.5.0-beta)?
1.10.3-beta

Java environment (e.g. Java 6, Android 2.3, App Engine)?
Java 6

Describe the problem.

FieldInfo, line ~97 calls setAccessible(true) on the Field.  This can cause 
problems in a JVM with a SecurityManager (e.g. 
java.security.AccessControlException: access denied 
(java.lang.reflect.ReflectPermission suppressAccessChecks)).

How would you expect it to be fixed?

First, that call should be guarded by an if block checking if the Field is 
already accessible (in which case there is no need for the call).

Second, it may be appropriate to just catch and swallow the SecurityException 
thrown by the setAccessible() call and allow the relevant Exception to be 
thrown in the future if the getFieldValue() or setFieldValue() methods are ever 
called.

So, maybe:

if(!field.isAccessible()) {
  try {
    field.setAccessible(true);
  } catch(SecurityException e) {
    // fail later in setFieldValue/getFieldValue
  }
}

```

issue.body:
1. The changes to the public API are extremely minor, it simply adds a new object, `KmlDataSource`, which is the same as other data sources but for KML. It only has 3 functions. (`fromUrl`, `load`, `loadUrl`).
2. Also adds KML and KMZ support to `viewerDragDropMixin` and the Cesium Viewer app `source` parameter.
3. I've been keeping #873 up to date with what's done and what's not for overall KML support, check that out if you want to see what we support/don't support yet.
4. Do not look at `SurfacePositionProperty` at yet, I still have a lot of work to do on this class (including renaming it).  I'll update this PR when it's ready.  No matter what, it will be private for 1.7 since we still need to figure out the exact details of height reference support.  This is more about laying ground work.

Also, just a reminder that you'll want to either set `InfoBoxViewModel.defaultSanitizer` to `undefined` or comment out line 161 of `InfoBoxViewModel` when you're playing with this in order to avoid balloon descriptions getting neutered. I plan on addressing this in an unrelated pull (hopefully before 1.7).  You'll also want to use the proxy if you play with public Network Links.

- [x] Verify how styles are applied and write tests for each type of Entity that gets created.
- [x] Test DataSource clock and changed/error/loading events
- [x] Replace Sandcastle example and sample KML data, also snap new gallery image.
- [x] Update CHANGES
- [x] Improve ref doc and explain the `Entity.kml` property that gets added.

issue.title: MediaHttpUploader.upload() requires a known InputStreamContent size
issue.body:
```
Version of google-api-java-client (e.g. 1.5.0-beta)?
1.10.3-beta

Java environment (e.g. Java 6, Android 2.3, App Engine)?
Java 6

Describe the problem.
If you provide an InputStreamContent where you've not specified setLength(), 
and thus it defaults to -1 (unknown length), you get a precondition failed:

java.lang.IllegalArgumentException
	at com.google.common.base.Preconditions.checkArgument(Preconditions.java:72)
	at com.google.api.client.googleapis.media.MediaHttpUploader.getMediaContentLength(MediaHttpUploader.java:315)
	at com.google.api.client.googleapis.media.MediaHttpUploader.executeUploadInitiation(MediaHttpUploader.java:333)
	at com.google.api.client.googleapis.media.MediaHttpUploader.upload(MediaHttpUploader.java:252)


How would you expect it to be fixed?
1) MediaHttpUploader.getMediaContentLength() should remove the precondition.
2) MediaHttpUploader.executeUploadInitiation should 
setUploadContentLength(null) (or if omitting that header doesn't work, there 
should be an overload that allows a "X-Upload-Content-Length: *", which is how 
you specify an unknown length to the upload service).
3) MediaHttpUploader.setContentAndHeadersOnCurrentRequest should specify the 
Content-Range ending in * when getMediaContentLength() == -1. It also needs to 
change its blockSize calculation in the case getMediaContentLength() == -1 to 
try to read the whole block and if you reach the end of the stream, 
setMediaContentLength() to be the appropriate value.
4) I'm not sure this is required, but you may end up having to additionally add 
X-Upload-Content-Length: * in the setContentAndHeadersOnCurrentRequest until 
such time as you resolve the end of the stream. 
```

issue.title: MediaHttpUploader.upload() requires a known InputStreamContent size
issue.body:
```
Version of google-api-java-client (e.g. 1.5.0-beta)?
1.10.3-beta

Java environment (e.g. Java 6, Android 2.3, App Engine)?
Java 6

Describe the problem.
If you provide an InputStreamContent where you've not specified setLength(), 
and thus it defaults to -1 (unknown length), you get a precondition failed:

java.lang.IllegalArgumentException
	at com.google.common.base.Preconditions.checkArgument(Preconditions.java:72)
	at com.google.api.client.googleapis.media.MediaHttpUploader.getMediaContentLength(MediaHttpUploader.java:315)
	at com.google.api.client.googleapis.media.MediaHttpUploader.executeUploadInitiation(MediaHttpUploader.java:333)
	at com.google.api.client.googleapis.media.MediaHttpUploader.upload(MediaHttpUploader.java:252)


How would you expect it to be fixed?
1) MediaHttpUploader.getMediaContentLength() should remove the precondition.
2) MediaHttpUploader.executeUploadInitiation should 
setUploadContentLength(null) (or if omitting that header doesn't work, there 
should be an overload that allows a "X-Upload-Content-Length: *", which is how 
you specify an unknown length to the upload service).
3) MediaHttpUploader.setContentAndHeadersOnCurrentRequest should specify the 
Content-Range ending in * when getMediaContentLength() == -1. It also needs to 
change its blockSize calculation in the case getMediaContentLength() == -1 to 
try to read the whole block and if you reach the end of the stream, 
setMediaContentLength() to be the appropriate value.
4) I'm not sure this is required, but you may end up having to additionally add 
X-Upload-Content-Length: * in the setContentAndHeadersOnCurrentRequest until 
such time as you resolve the end of the stream. 
```

issue.title: Ensure exceptions from methodBlock() don't result in unrooted tests
issue.body:
The introduction of the runLeaf() method in BlockJUnit4ClassRunner in
JUnit 4.9 introduced a regression with regard to exception handling.

Specifically, the invocation of methodBlock() is no longer executed
within a try-catch block as was the case in previous versions of JUnit.

Custom modifications to methodBlock() or the methods it invokes may in
fact throw exceptions. In such cases, exceptions thrown from
methodBlock() cause the current test execution to abort immediately. As
a result, the failing test method is unrooted in test reports, and
subsequent test methods are never invoked. Furthermore, RunListeners
registered with JUnit are not notified.

This commit addresses this issue by wrapping the invocation of
methodBlock() within a try-catch block. If an exception is not thrown,
the resulting Statement is passed to runLeaf(). If an exception is
thrown, it is wrapped in a Fail statement which is passed to runLeaf().

Issue: #1066

issue.title: Remove Line for iTunesArtwork Problem
issue.body:
Recently Apple have made some changes and when submitting ipa to app store we get 

![81p0ymfhkegss8rwatma](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/184276/4019848/3ffd62da-2a8e-11e4-975e-eb548b834d77.png)


To solve issue we need to remove line on rake file. 



https://github.com/rhomobile/rhodes/blob/49ea6b4e8a951a26057f0b4f4bb91ebf7a93815e/platform/iphone/rbuild/iphone.rake#L350

Best regards

comment.body:
Try this:

issue.title: remove getResponseHeaders() from model classes [backwards incompatible]
issue.body:
```
External references, such as a standards document, or specification?

http://javadoc.google-api-java-client.googlecode.com/hg/apis/calendar/v3/com/goo
gle/api/services/calendar/model/Calendar.html#getResponseHeaders()

http://javadoc.google-http-java-client.googlecode.com/hg/1.11.0-beta/com/google/
api/client/http/json/JsonHttpRequest.html?is-external=true#getLastResponseHeader
s()

Java environments (e.g. Java 6, Android 2.3, App Engine, or All)?

All

Please describe the feature requested.

Some model classes -- such as com.google.api.services.calendar.model.Calendar 
-- have a getResponseHeaders() method.  This unnecessarily adds a dependency on 
HTTP headers into the model classes.  It is also usually redundant.  One can 
instead call getEtag() directly from the JSON model class if that's available, 
or more generally use request.getLastResponseHeaders().

For example, instead of:

responseObject.getResponseHeaders().getETag()

you can normally just do:

responseObject.getETag()

or more generally:

requestObject.getLastResponseHeaders().getETag()

So this is a backwards-incompatible change to remove getResponseHeaders() from 
the JSON model classes.
```

release.name: Wharf - Open Source ContainerOps Platform
release.body:
## Wharf - Open Source ContainerOps Platform

Wharf is a successor of ContainerOps platform whose concept is built upon the DevOps, which means it's a higher level solution over traditional approach and DevOps, but not an alternative. The ultimate goal of Wharf is building a pipeline form development to deployment & operations through Docker, Rocket and other container solutions.

ContainerOps is all about product workflow. Wharf builds and runs a container image you defined whenever new code is being pushed, along with corresponding dependence system. But it's not all, the image will also work with continuous integration, or continuous deployment with Rocket, LXC or Atomic, etc. Wharf is focusing on the continuous changes from version control system to production environment.

Now, it's time to announce our pre-release and core of ContainerOps version of Wharf, you can replace Docker Registry with it. Please make sure you know that Wharf is currently under alpha stage.

Our team is still working really hard for your happiness with the complete version of ContainerOps platform, which comes in next few months.

## Changelog

* Registry user from web `/auth`.
* User profile and password.
* Management organization with teams and members.
* Full support Docker Registry V1.

## The Feature TODO

1. Docker Registry V2 support.
2. Docker Hub repository sync automatically.
3. Rocket **CAS** support.
4. More relative pages.

## Project

You can find Wharf on [GitHub](https://github.com/dockercn/wharf).

## How To Run Wharf

https://github.com/dockercn/wharf/wiki/How-To-Run-Wharf

## Reporting Issues

Please submit issues at [GitHub](https://github.com/dockercn/wharf/issues).

## Core Maintainers

- [Meaglith Ma](https://twitter.com/genedna)
- [Allen Chen](https://github.com/chliang2030598)
- [Leo Meng](https://github.com/fivestarsky)
- [Unknwon](https://github.com/Unknwon)

## License

Wharf is licensed under the MIT License.

## Wharf-related Projects

We are also working on other Wharf-related projects:

* [Vessel](https://githbu.com/dockercn/vessel): a continuous integration system build with Docker.
* [Rudder](https://github.com/dockercn/rudder): a Docker client for Golang.

issue.title: Ensure exceptions from methodBlock() don't result in unrooted tests
issue.body:
The introduction of the runLeaf() method in BlockJUnit4ClassRunner in
JUnit 4.9 introduced a regression with regard to exception handling.

Specifically, the invocation of methodBlock() is no longer executed
within a try-catch block as was the case in previous versions of JUnit.

Custom modifications to methodBlock() or the methods it invokes may in
fact throw exceptions. In such cases, exceptions thrown from
methodBlock() cause the current test execution to abort immediately. As
a result, the failing test method is unrooted in test reports, and
subsequent test methods are never invoked. Furthermore, RunListeners
registered with JUnit are not notified.

This commit addresses this issue by wrapping the invocation of
methodBlock() within a try-catch block. If an exception is not thrown,
the resulting Statement is passed to runLeaf(). If an exception is
thrown, it is wrapped in a Fail statement which is passed to runLeaf().

Issue: #1066

comment.body: @sbrannen do you mind updating the JUnit 4.13 release notes to mention this pull?

issue.title: Batch requests should allow null callbacks
issue.body:
```
Version of google-api-java-client (e.g. 1.5.0-beta)?

HEAD


Java environment (e.g. Java 6, Android 2.3, App Engine)?

App Engine


Describe the problem.

I'd like to perform a batch request, but I don't particularly care about the 
respective responses. I essentially want to "fire and forget" a series of API 
requests.

Currently I'm calling:

BatchRequest batch = compute.batch();
for (...) {
  compute.instances().insert(...).queue(batch, null);
}
batch.execute();

This results in an NPE because of a Preconditions.checkNotNull check on the 
callback:
java.lang.NullPointerException
	at com.google.common.base.Preconditions.checkNotNull(Preconditions.java:193)
	at com.google.api.client.googleapis.batch.BatchRequest.queue(BatchRequest.java:161)
	at com.google.api.services.compute.Compute$Instances$Insert.queue(Compute.java:2642)




How would you expect it to be fixed?

Either remove the checkNotNull check, or provide another queue() method that 
doesn't take a callback. Ideally requests that don't configure a callback would 
also skip parsing of the response entirely, since nothing downstream requires 
any details of the response.

This would lead to clearer more succinct code than the current working 
alternative, which is to define a no-op JsonBatchCallback instance that does 
nothing.
```

issue.title: Using Login with Origin Security Code
issue.body:
When trying to login, origin always wants a security code that is send via mail.
How do you handle that?

Greetings.

comment.body:
As far as I'm aware, there are two ways:
Either you design a way for PHP to search your mail, extract the code and use it (Shouldn't be too hard, there are a lot of mail PHP plugins already available) 
-- Or --
Use Origins Backup codes (Gives you 6 tries before needing more) This is the easiest approach since I have managed to go days without a disconnect.

Be aware the Web App's transfer market is currently down so once you log in there isn't much to do.

  public HttpRequest buildHttpRequestUsingHead() throws Exception

resource JSON content.  So you'll be able to call 
subscribe(...).executeUsingHead().

1. Class selection fails unless it's death by a car or something client-side.

3. Is the death world thing necessary? It seems to inflict bugs than anything else.

**Suggestion**

1. Allow users to easily disable portions of the code with using #define instead of using functions (Toggle{function}(bool: value)

    ```
#define TOGGLE_DAMAGE_FEED (true)

#if TOGGLE_DAMAGE_FEED == true
 ... operations ...
#endif

issue.title: Smarter handling of OAuth 2 failures when getting a 401 error
issue.body:
```
We recently had an error reported of a "401 Unauthorized" error when trying to 
access a Google API endpoint.  It kept refreshing the access token, trying to 
access the Google API, got a 401 error, and then continue the loop until 
reaching the max retry number.  It then simply threw an exception.  We don't 
the root cause of the problem, but one guess is that it may have been that the 
token didn't have the right scopes defined for the API method.

Ideally the client library could help in determining the problem using the 
tokeninfo endpoint which gives information about access tokens.  So for example 
if we know what scopes are required by an API method, and we get a 401 error, 
we could ask tokeninfo to tell us if the access token is valid and what scopes 
it has defined.  If we see that it doesn't have the appropriate scope for 
example, we could throw a more descriptive error explaining the problem, and 
not attempt to refresh the token and retry the request.
```

expiration (e.g., if the resource is modified/deleted and the SeekableStream 
has to go to the service for more data -- perhaps it throws some kind of 
exception in those cases, or rather it flows gracefully to the next version)

Original issue reported on code.google.com by `yan...@google.com` on 16 Oct 2012 at 10:08

comment.body:
```
Nah, let's drop this general-purpose header setting idea.  If there are headers 
that are commonly set, we should just add utility methods to help set this.

So in this case, to solve the etag case we should add setIfMatchHeader:

client.calendars().delete(calendar.getId())
    .setIfMatchHeader("someEtag")
    .execute()

So we should generate setIfMatchHeader to all PUT, PATCH, & DELETE API methods.

Similarly, we should generate setIfNoneMatchHeader to all GET API methods.

Note that POST API methods do not have ETag.  I'm guessing other HTTP methods 
don't have it either.  Regardless, this is just a convenience, since you can 
always access getRequestHeaders().
```

e.api.client.googleapis.GoogleHeaders)

All

Please describe the feature requested.

When doing resumable media upload, I can call setInitiationHeaders to provide 
arbitrary headers to add to the metadata request.  This enables the ability for 
example to add subscriptions headers.

However, there is no way to supply additional headers when 
setDirectUploadEnabled(true), so there is no way for example to subscribe while 
doing direct media upload.

This feature request is to use the same initiation headers when 
setDirectUploadEnabled(true).  Alternatively, provide some other way to set 
those headers.
